category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: What is the minimum symptom duration required for the diagnosis of Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: 6 weeks.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Criteria for diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis... Duration of symptoms > 6 weeks].

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: Which specific signaling molecule mediates osteoclast activation and bone erosions in Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: RANKL (produced by activated T cells).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1086 (Book Page): [A key pathogenic factor in bone erosions... is osteoclast activation, stimulated by the production of... RANKL by activated T cells].

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: Contrast the hand joint involvement of Rheumatoid Arthritis with Osteoarthritis.
back: RA typically targets MCP and PIP joints but spares the Distal Interphalangeal (DIP) joints.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [typical presentation is with pain, joint swelling and stiffness affecting the small joints of the hands... in a symmetrical fashion. (Figure 26.10 spares DIP)].

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: An RA patient presents with occipital headache and electric shock sensations in the arms. What is the diagnosis?
back: Atlanto-axial subluxation (Cervical cord compression).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): [should be suspected in any RA patient who describes new onset of occipital headache... symptoms of paraesthesia or electric shock are present in the arms].

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: Which conventional synthetic DMARD (cDMARD) is the gold-standard first-line treatment for Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: Methotrexate (MTX).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1091 (Book Page): [methotrexate (MTX) should be started in an initial dose of 15 mg weekly].

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: List the four categories evaluated in the 2010 ACR/EULAR criteria for RA classification.
back:
* Joint involvement
* Serology (RF/ACPA)
* Acute phase reactants (CRP/ESR)
* Duration of symptoms.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Criteria for diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis... Joint involvement, Serology, Duration, Acute phase reactants].

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: How is a ruptured Baker’s cyst clinically differentiated from Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT) in an RA patient?
back: Rupture causes sudden calf pain and swelling mimicking DVT; ultrasound is required for differentiation.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Rupture may be induced by knee flexion, leading to calf pain and swelling that may mimic a deep venous thrombosis].

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: What triad of findings defines Felty Syndrome in long-standing Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back:
1. Rheumatoid Arthritis
2. Splenomegaly
3. Neutropenia.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): [Box 26.54 Felty Syndrome: Splenomegaly, Neutropenia... Long-standing rheumatoid arthritis].

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: Which cytokine triggers the hepatic production of acute phase proteins (CRP/ESR) in Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: Interleukin-6 (IL-6).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1086 (Book Page): [Systemic release of IL-6 triggers production of acute phase proteins by the liver].

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: Between Rheumatoid Factor (RF) and Anti-CCP (ACPA), which has higher specificity for diagnosing RA?
back: Anti-CCP (ACPA) is highly specific for RA and may be present before clinical onset.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): [Tests for ACPA... are highly specific for RA... RF is less specific than ACPA].

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: What is the typical clinical distribution of joint involvement in Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: Symmetrical involvement of small joints, primarily targeting the hands, feet, and wrists.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1086 (Book Page): Typical presentation is with pain, joint swelling and stiffness affecting the small joints of the hands, feet and wrists in a symmetrical fashion.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: What are the primary pro-inflammatory cytokines driving synovial macrophage activation in RA?
back: TNF-alpha, IL-1, and IL-6; these establish a positive feedback loop with synovial fibroblasts.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1086 (Book Page): The macrophages produce several pro-inflammatory cytokines, including TNF-α, IL-1 and IL-6, which act on synovial fibroblasts to produce further cytokines.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: How is the thumb's 'Z-deformity' distinguished from finger deformities in RA?
back: Z-deformity specifically involves the thumb, whereas Swan-neck and Boutonnière involve the other fingers.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): They include ulnar deviation of the fingers, ‘swan neck’ deformity, the boutonnière or ‘buttonhole’ deformity and a Z deformity of the thumb.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: A patient with long-standing RA presents with occipital headache and paresthesia. Diagnosis?
back: Atlanto-axial subluxation; caused by erosion of the transverse ligament posterior to the odontoid peg.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): It should be suspected in any RA patient who describes new onset of occipital headache, particularly if symptoms of paraesthesia... are present.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: What is the first-line DMARD therapy and dose for a newly diagnosed RA patient?
back: Methotrexate (15mg weekly) combined with folic acid (5mg weekly).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): methotrexate (MTX) should be started in an initial dose of 15 mg weekly, along with folic acid 5 mg weekly.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: List the four main categories used in the ACR/EULAR 2010 classification criteria for RA.
back: 1. Joint involvement; 2. Serology (RF/ACPA); 3. Acute phase reactants (CRP/ESR); 4. Duration (≥6 weeks).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): Criteria for diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis: Joints affected, Serology, Duration of symptoms, Acute phase reactants.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Define 'Palindromic Rheumatism' as an initial presentation of Rheumatoid Arthritis.
back: Relapsing/remitting episodes of pain, stiffness, and swelling lasting only hours or days.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1086 (Book Page): The onset is palindromic, with relapsing and remitting episodes of pain, stiffness and swelling that last for only a few hours or days.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Identify the clinical triad of Felty Syndrome occurring as a complication of RA.
back: 1. Long-standing RA; 2. Splenomegaly; 3. Neutropenia.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): Felty syndrome is a rare complication of seropositive RA in which splenomegaly occurs in combination with neutropenia.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: What is the specific mechanism for marginal bone erosion in Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: Pannus invades bone through osteoclast activation via RANKL and M-CSF signaling.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1086 (Book Page): Inflamed synovium (pannus) directly invades bone and cartilage... key pathogenic factor in bone erosions... is osteoclast activation, stimulated by... RANKL.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Which autoantibody is highly specific for RA and identifies patients before clinical onset?
back: Anti-citrullinated peptide antibody (ACPA).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): Tests for ACPA are positive in about 70% of cases and are highly specific for RA, occurring in many patients before clinical onset.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: What are the hallmark clinical features and joint distribution for a typical Rheumatoid Arthritis presentation?
back:
• Symmetrical inflammatory polyarthritis.
• Primarily involves small joints: MCPs, PIPs, wrists, and MTPs.
• Clinical hallmarks: Joint pain, swelling, and severe early morning stiffness.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1086 (Book Page): 'The typical presentation is with pain, joint swelling and stiffness affecting the small joints of the hands, feet and wrists in a symmetrical fashion.'

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Which specific cellular signaling pathway drives the marginal bone erosions characteristic of Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back:
• Inflamed synovium (pannus) directly invades bone at joint margins.
• Osteoclast activation is the primary driver.
• Mediated by M-CSF from synovial cells and RANKL from activated T-cells.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1086 (Book Page): 'At the joint margin, the inflamed synovium (pannus) directly invades bone and cartilage to cause joint erosions. A key pathogenic factor... is osteoclast activation, stimulated by the production of M-CSF by synovial cells and RANKL by activated T cells.'

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: According to EULAR/ACR 2010 criteria, which four clinical and laboratory domains define Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back:
• Joint Involvement: Number and site of joints affected.
• Serology: Rheumatoid Factor (RF) or ACPA.
• Acute Phase Reactants: Elevated CRP or ESR.
• Duration: Symptoms lasting ≥6 weeks.
• Score ≥6/10 confirms RA.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): 'Box 26.52 Criteria for diagnosis... Joints affected... Serology... Duration of symptoms... Acute phase reactants... Patients with a score ≥ 6 are considered to have definite RA.'

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: What is the characteristic joint distribution of Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA)?
back:
• Symmetrical polyarthritis
• Small joints (MCP, PIP, MTP)
• Wrists and feet
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1086 (Book Page): [Typical presentation is with pain, joint swelling and stiffness affecting the small joints of the hands, feet and wrists in a symmetrical fashion.]

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: What is the primary mechanism of bone erosion at the joint margin in RA?
back:
• RANKL production by activated T-cells
• Activation of osteoclasts
• Direct invasion by inﬂamed synovium (pannus)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1086 (Book Page): [A key pathogenic factor in bone erosions... is osteoclast activation, stimulated by... RANKL by activated T cells.]

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: How does the duration of morning stiffness differentiate RA from Osteoarthritis (OA)?
back:
• RA: Severe and prolonged (>30–60 mins)
• OA: Mild and brief (<15 mins)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [RA has acute onset, with severe early morning stiffness...] compared to Page 1074 (Book Page) [OA has mild morning stiffness < 15 mins].

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: A long-standing RA patient presents with a new occipital headache and arm paraesthesia. Likely diagnosis?
back:
• Atlanto-axial subluxation
• Cervical cord compression
• Requires urgent neurosurgical referral
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): [suspected in any RA patient who describes new onset of occipital headache... Atlanto-axial subluxation is due to erosion of the transverse ligament.]

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: What is the standard 'Triple Therapy' DMARD regimen for UHS rheumatology protocols?
back:
• Methotrexate (MTX)
• Sulfasalazine (SSZ)
• Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): [A common combination is triple therapy, in which MTX, SSZ and HCQ are combined.]

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: What are the four scoring domains of the 2010 EULAR/ACR RA criteria?
back:
1. Joint involvement
2. Serology (RF or ACPA)
3. Acute phase reactants (CRP or ESR)
4. Duration of symptoms
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Criteria for diagnosis of RA: Joints affected, Serology, Duration of symptoms, Acute phase reactants.]

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: Why is ACPA (Anti-CCP) testing clinically preferred over Rheumatoid Factor (RF)?
back:
• ACPA is highly specific for RA
• RF is less specific (found in other infections/diseases)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): [Tests for ACPA... are highly specific for RA... RF is less specific than ACPA, however, and positive tests can occur in other diseases.]

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: An RA patient with knee synovitis develops sudden calf pain and swelling. What must you exclude?
back:
• Ruptured Popliteal (Baker's) cyst
• Deep Venous Thrombosis (DVT)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Rupture may be induced by knee flexion, leading to calf pain and swelling that may mimic a deep venous thrombosis (DVT).]

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: Which cytokine triggers the hepatic production of acute phase reactants (CRP) in RA?
back:
• Interleukin-6 (IL-6)
• Released systemically during inflammation
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1086 (Book Page): [Systemic release of IL-6 triggers production of acute phase proteins by the liver.]

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: Which entrapment neuropathy is most commonly associated with active RA?
back:
• Median nerve compression
• Carpal Tunnel Syndrome
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): [Median nerve compression is the most common and bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome can occur as a presenting feature of RA.]

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: What are the characteristic joints first affected in Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back:
- Symmetrical small joints: MCP, PIP, MTP, and wrists.
- Usually presents with pain, swelling, and morning stiffness.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1086 (Book Page): The typical presentation is with pain, joint swelling and stiffness affecting the small joints of the hands, feet and wrists in a symmetrical fashion.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Explain the 'positive feedback loop' involving macrophages in RA synovial inflammation.
back:
- Macrophages produce TNF-α, IL-1, and IL-6.
- These activate synovial fibroblasts to produce more cytokines and matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1086 (Book Page): The macrophages produce several pro-inflammatory cytokines, including TNF-α, IL-1 and IL-6, which act on synovial fibroblasts to produce further cytokines, setting up a positive feedback loop.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: How does joint involvement in the hands contrast between RA and nodal Osteoarthritis?
back:
- RA: Affects MCPs and PIPs; spares the DIP joints.
- OA: Targets DIPs (Heberden's) and PIPs (Bouchard's).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [RA] criteria includes... 1–3 small joints... [Page 1074 (Book Page): Nodal OA targets] Heberden’s (DIP) and Bouchard’s (PIP) nodes.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: An RA patient presents with occipital headache and limb paresthesia. What life-threatening complication is suspected?
back:
- Atlanto-axial subluxation.
- Erosion of the transverse ligament leads to spinal cord compression or sudden death.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): Atlanto-axial subluxation is due to erosion of the transverse ligament... It should be suspected in any RA patient who describes new onset of occipital headache.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Which specific molecules drive osteoclast activation and marginal bone erosions in RA?
back:
- RANKL (produced by activated T cells).
- M-CSF (produced by synovial cells).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1086 (Book Page): A key pathogenic factor in bone erosions... is osteoclast activation, stimulated by the production of M-CSF by synovial cells and RANKL by activated T cells.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: What is the minimum score required for a definite RA diagnosis using 2010 ACR/EULAR criteria?
back:
- A total score of ≥ 6 points.
- Calculated based on joint involvement, serology (RF/ACPA), duration, and acute phase reactants.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): Patients with a score ≥ 6 are considered to have definite RA.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Identify the classic hand deformities associated with long-standing, uncontrolled RA.
back:
- Ulnar deviation of fingers.
- Swan neck deformity.
- Boutonnière deformity.
- Z-deformity of the thumb.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): They include ulnar deviation of the fingers, ‘swan neck’ deformity, the boutonnière or ‘buttonhole’ deformity and a Z deformity of the thumb.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: A patient with knee synovitis develops sudden calf pain/swelling. What is the most likely RA-related differential?
back:
- Ruptured Popliteal (Baker's) cyst.
- Mimics Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT) due to fluid tracking down the calf.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): Rupture may be induced by knee flexion, leading to calf pain and swelling that may mimic a deep venous thrombosis (DVT).

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: What are the primary extra-articular pulmonary manifestations of seropositive RA?
back:
- Pleural effusions and serositis.
- Pulmonary fibrosis.
- Rheumatoid nodules.
- Caplan syndrome (nodules with pneumoconiosis).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1088 (Book Page): Pulmonary fibrosis may occur... [Page 1088 (Book Page): Box 26.53] Pleural effusions, Pulmonary fibrosis, Caplan syndrome.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Compare the diagnostic utility of Rheumatoid Factor (RF) and Anti-Cyclic Citrullinated Peptide (ACPA).
back:
- Both ~70% sensitive.
- ACPA: Highly specific for RA.
- RF: Less specific; can occur in other diseases.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): Tests for ACPA are positive in about 70% of cases and are highly specific for RA... RF is less specific than ACPA.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: Which joint distribution pattern is most characteristic of early Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back:
- Symmetrical involvement.
- Targets small joints of hands, feet, and wrists.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [The typical presentation is with pain, joint swelling and stiffness affecting the small joints of the hands, feet and wrists in a symmetrical fashion.]

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: What primary cellular mechanism drives bone erosions at the joint margin in RA?
back:
- Osteoclast activation.
- Stimulated by RANKL (from T cells) and M-CSF (synovial cells) within the pannus.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [A key pathogenic factor in bone erosions and periarticular osteoporosis is osteoclast activation, stimulated by the production of M-CSF by synovial cells and RANKL by activated T cells.]

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: How do RA and Osteoarthritis differ in the duration of morning stiffness?
back:
- RA: Severe, prolonged stiffness (often >1 hour).
- OA: Mild stiffness (<15 mins) and inactivity gelling (<5 mins).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Sometimes RA has an acute onset, with severe early morning stiffness...]; Page 1074 (Book Page): [Mild morning stiffness ( < 15 mins) and inactivity gelling ( < 5 mins) after rest]

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: A patient with long-standing RA presents with occipital headache and arm paresthesia; what complication is suspected?
back:
- Atlanto-axial subluxation.
- Caused by erosion of the transverse ligament posterior to the odontoid peg.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): [It should be suspected in any RA patient who describes new onset of occipital headache, particularly if symptoms of paraesthesia or electric shock are present in the arms.]

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: In the initial management of RA, why is folic acid co-prescribed with Methotrexate?
back:
- To reduce dose-limiting toxicity of Methotrexate.
- Standard initial dose: 15mg MTX/week with 5mg folic acid/week.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1091 (Book Page): [methotrexate (MTX) should be started in an initial dose of 15 mg weekly, along with folic acid 5 mg weekly, and escalated up to a maximum of 25 mg weekly, depending on the response.]

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: What four core domains are assessed in the 2010 EULAR/ACR classification criteria for RA?
back:
1. Joint involvement.
2. Serology (RF or ACPA).
3. Duration of symptoms (≥6 weeks).
4. Acute phase reactants (CRP or ESR).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1088 (Book Page): [Box 26.52: Criteria for diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis... Joints affected, Serology, Duration of symptoms, Acute phase reactants.]

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: Describe the characteristic 'Swan neck' and 'Boutonnière' hand deformities in chronic RA.
back:
- Swan neck: PIP hyperextension with DIP flexion.
- Boutonnière: PIP flexion with DIP hyperextension.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1088 (Book Page): [They include ulnar deviation of the fingers, ‘swan neck’ deformity, the boutonnière or ‘buttonhole’ deformity and a Z deformity of the thumb.]

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: Which clinical triad defines Felty Syndrome as a complication of long-standing RA?
back:
1. Rheumatoid Arthritis.
2. Splenomegaly.
3. Neutropenia.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): [Felty syndrome is a rare complication of seropositive RA in which splenomegaly occurs in combination with neutropenia and thrombocytopenia.]

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: How do macrophages and synovial fibroblasts perpetuate the inflammatory loop in RA?
back:
- Macrophages produce TNF-α, IL-1, and IL-6.
- These activate fibroblasts to produce further cytokines and matrix metalloproteinases.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [The synovial macrophages are activated by TNF-α and interferon-gamma (IFN-γ)... produce several pro-inflammatory cytokines... act on synovial fibroblasts to produce further cytokines, setting up a positive feedback loop.]

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: What serious clinical condition is often mimicked by a ruptured Baker’s cyst in an RA patient?
back:
- Deep Venous Thrombosis (DVT).
- Presents with sudden calf pain and swelling.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1088 (Book Page): [Rupture may be induced by knee flexion, leading to calf pain and swelling that may mimic a deep venous thrombosis (DVT).]

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: What is the typical joint distribution and pattern in Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA)?
back: Symmetrical involvement of small joints, specifically the hands, feet, and wrists.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1086 (Book Page): The typical presentation is with pain, joint swelling and stiffness affecting the small joints of the hands, feet and wrists in a symmetrical fashion.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Why is systemic IL-6 release significant in the clinical monitoring of RA?
back: It triggers liver production of acute phase proteins, resulting in elevated CRP and ESR.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1086 (Book Page): Systemic release of IL-6 triggers production of acute phase proteins by the liver.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: How does RA morning stiffness differentiate clinically from Osteoarthritis (OA)?
back: RA stiffness is severe and prolonged (often >1 hour), while OA stiffness is brief (<15 minutes).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1086 (Book Page): RA has an acute onset, with severe early morning stiffness... Page 1074 (Book Page): [OA] Mild morning stiffness (< 15 mins).

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: An RA patient presents with sudden calf pain and swelling. What clinical mimic must be excluded?
back: Ruptured Popliteal (Baker’s) cyst, which mimics Deep Venous Thrombosis (DVT).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): Rupture [of Baker's cyst] may be induced by knee flexion, leading to calf pain and swelling that may mimic a deep venous thrombosis (DVT).

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Which autoantibody is highly specific for RA and may precede clinical onset?
back: Anti-citrullinated peptide antibody (ACPA).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): Tests for ACPA are positive in about 70% of cases and are highly specific for RA, occurring in many patients before clinical onset of the disease.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: What is the threshold score for 'definite RA' under the EULAR/ACR 2010 criteria?
back: A total score of ≥ 6.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): Patients with a score ≥ 6 are considered to have definite RA.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: List three characteristic hand deformities resulting from long-standing uncontrolled RA.
back:
1. Swan neck deformity
2. Boutonnière deformity
3. Z-deformity of the thumb
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): They include ulnar deviation of the fingers, ‘swan neck’ deformity, the boutonnière or ‘buttonhole’ deformity and a Z deformity of the thumb.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: An RA patient develops occipital headache and arm paresthesia. What is the urgent differential?
back: Atlanto-axial subluxation causing cervical spinal cord compression.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): It should be suspected in any RA patient who describes new onset of occipital headache... paresthesia or electric shock are present in the arms.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Describe the clinical significance of finding erythema in a suspected RA joint.
back: Erythema is unusual in RA; its presence strongly suggests coexistent infection (septic arthritis).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): Erythema is unusual and its presence suggests coexistent infection.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Which specific joint group of the hand is classically spared in Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: The Distal Interphalangeal (DIP) joints.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1086 (Book Page): [RA affects] small joints of the hands... [Context: unlike OA which targets DIPs per Page 1074 (Book Page)].

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Which specific joint pattern most clearly differentiates Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) from Osteoarthritis (OA)?
back: RA typically involves symmetrical small joints (MCP, PIP, MTP) and wrists, while OA targets weight-bearing joints (hips, knees) and the DIP joints.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1086 (Book Page): [Rheumatoid arthritis (RA)] typical presentation is with pain, joint swelling and stiffness affecting the small joints of the hands, feet and wrists in a symmetrical fashion.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: What is the significance of Citrullination in the pathophysiology of RA polyarthritis?
back: Environmental stimuli trigger citrullination of host proteins (modifying them), which then become immunogenic in genetically susceptible individuals (HLA-DRB1).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1086 (Book Page): [RA occurs when] an environmental stimulus... triggers autoimmunity... by modifying host proteins, through processes like citrullination, so that they become immunogenic.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Contrast the duration of morning stiffness in RA versus Osteoarthritis.
back:
RA: Prolonged morning stiffness (usually >1 hour). 
OA: Short-lived morning stiffness (<15 mins) and inactivity 'gelling' (<5 mins).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1074 (Book Page): [OA has] Mild morning stiffness (< 15 mins) and inactivity gelling (< 5 mins) after rest.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: A patient presents with 'sausage digits' (dactylitis). Which diagnosis does this favor over RA?
back: Psoriatic Arthritis (PsA) or Reactive Arthritis. Dactylitis is a hallmark of Spondyloarthritis (SpA), whereas RA features isolated joint synovitis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1092 (Book Page): A hallmark lesion of SpAs is enthesitis... Dactylitis, inflammation of a whole finger or toe, may also occur.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: What is the first-line disease-modifying treatment (DMARD) for confirmed RA?
back: Methotrexate (MTX) is the drug of first choice, typically started at 15 mg weekly and escalated up to 25 mg with folic acid supplementation.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): On first diagnosis... methotrexate (MTX) should be started in an initial dose of 15 mg weekly... and escalated up to a maximum of 25 mg weekly.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: According to the 2010 ACR/EULAR criteria, what score is required for a definite diagnosis of RA?
back: A score of ≥ 6 points is required, based on four domains: joint involvement, serology (RF/ACPA), duration of symptoms, and acute phase reactants (CRP/ESR).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Box 26.52] Patients with a score ≥ 6 are considered to have definite RA.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: How do RA nodules differ clinically from Gouty tophi?
back:
RA Nodules: Flesh-colored, occur on extensor surfaces. 
Tophi: White/chalky appearance, can discharge gritty material (urate crystals).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1079 (Book Page): Tophi have a white colour... differentiating them from rheumatoid nodules. Tophi can ulcerate, discharging white gritty material.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Differentiate RA from SLE-related arthritis based on radiographic findings.
back: RA is characterized by marginal bone erosions and joint space narrowing. SLE-related arthritis (Jaccoud’s) is typically non-erosive despite deformities.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1098 (Book Page): [In SLE] Joint deformities may arise... but joint erosions are not a feature.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: What laboratory marker is most specific for RA compared to Rheumatoid Factor (RF)?
back: Anti-citrullinated peptide antibody (ACPA). While RF is 70% sensitive, ACPA is highly specific and can precede clinical onset.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): Tests for ACPA are positive in about 70% of cases and are highly specific for RA... RF is less specific than ACPA.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Which finger deformities are classically associated with long-standing RA?
back: Swan-neck deformity (PIP hyperextension, DIP flexion) and Boutonnière deformity (PIP flexion, DIP hyperextension).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): They include ulnar deviation of the fingers, ‘swan neck’ deformity, the boutonnière or ‘buttonhole’ deformity.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: What is the characteristic clinical distribution of joint involvement in Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: Symmetrical involvement of small joints, primarily the hands (MCP, PIP), feet (MTP), and wrists.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1027 (Book Page): The typical presentation is with pain, joint swelling and stiffness affecting the small joints of the hands, feet and wrists in a symmetrical fashion.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: Which cytokine feedback loop involving macrophages drives synovial inflammation in RA?
back: Macrophages release TNF-α, IL-1, and IL-6, which stimulate synovial fibroblasts to produce more cytokines and matrix metalloproteinases.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1027 (Book Page): The macrophages produce several pro-inflammatory cytokines, including TNF-α, IL-1 and IL-6, which act on synovial fibroblasts to produce further cytokines, setting up a positive feedback loop.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: How does the hand joint involvement in RA contrast with nodal Osteoarthritis?
back: RA targets MCP and PIP joints (sparing DIPs), whereas nodal OA targets DIP (Heberden’s) and PIP (Bouchard’s) joints.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1028 (Book Page): [Fig 26.34] shows synovial swelling at the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints. Page 1015 (Book Page): become Heberden’s (DIP) and Bouchard’s (PIP) nodes.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: An RA patient presents with occipital headache and arm paraesthesia. What is the suspected complication?
back: Atlanto-axial subluxation leading to cervical spinal cord compression.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1030 (Book Page): It should be suspected in any RA patient who describes new onset of occipital headache, particularly if symptoms of paraesthesia or electric shock are present in the arms.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: What is the standard 'bridge therapy' used when initiating Methotrexate for new RA?
back: Glucocorticoids (e.g., Prednisolone 30mg daily) tapered and withdrawn over roughly 12 weeks.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1031 (Book Page): on first diagnosis, prednisolone can be started in a dose of 30 mg daily gradually reducing... until therapy is withdrawn after about 12 weeks.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: What minimum total score is required on the 2010 EULAR/ACR criteria for definite RA?
back: A score of ≥ 6 is required.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1028 (Book Page): Patients with a score ≥ 6 are considered to have definite RA.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: Which three classic hand deformities are hallmarks of advanced, uncontrolled RA?
back:
1. Ulnar deviation of fingers
2. Swan neck deformity
3. Boutonnière (buttonhole) deformity
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1028 (Book Page): They include ulnar deviation of the fingers, ‘swan neck’ deformity, the boutonnière or ‘buttonhole’ deformity.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: An RA patient with knee synovitis has sudden calf pain and swelling. What is the likely differential for DVT?
back: Ruptured Baker’s (popliteal) cyst.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1028 (Book Page): Rupture may be induced by knee flexion, leading to calf pain and swelling that may mimic a deep venous thrombosis (DVT).

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: Which cell type and ligand drive the marginal bone erosions seen in RA imaging?
back: Osteoclasts, activated by RANKL (produced by activated T cells) and M-CSF.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1027 (Book Page): A key pathogenic factor in bone erosions... is osteoclast activation, stimulated by the production of M-CSF by synovial cells and RANKL by activated T cells.

category: Diagnose RA based on characteristic clinical features
front: Q: Where are rheumatoid nodules typically found, and which patients are at risk?
back: Found on extensor surfaces (tendons/elbows); almost exclusive to RF or ACPA-positive patients.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1029 (Book Page): Rheumatoid nodules occur almost exclusively in RF- or ACPA-positive patients, usually in extensor tendons.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: What is the most specific autoantibody for differentiating Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) from other polyarthropathies?
back:
- Anti-Citrullinated Peptide Antibody (ACPA).
- Positive in ~70% of cases.
- Highly specific for RA diagnosis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1028 (Book Page): [Tests for ACPA are positive in about 70% of cases and are highly specific for RA, occurring in many patients before clinical onset of the disease.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Which cytokine and signaling pathway primarily drive the bone erosions characteristic of RA?
back:
- Interleukin-6 (IL-6) and TNF-α.
- Mechanism: RANKL and M-CSF stimulate osteoclast activation.
- Result: Marginal bone erosions and periarticular osteoporosis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1027 (Book Page): [A key pathogenic factor in bone erosions and periarticular osteoporosis is osteoclast activation, stimulated by the production of M-CSF by synovial cells and RANKL by activated T cells.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Differentiate RA from Osteoarthritis (OA) based on the duration and nature of morning stiffness.
back:
- RA: Symmetrical, inflammatory stiffness lasting >60 minutes.
- OA: Mild stiffness (<15 mins) and 'inactivity gelling' (<5 mins) after rest.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1074 (Book Page): [Typical OA pain... Mild morning stiffness ( < 15 mins) and inactivity gelling ( < 5 mins) after rest.] vs Page 1086 (Book Page): [The typical presentation is with pain, joint swelling and stiffness... in a symmetrical fashion.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: A 50-year-old female presents with symmetric hand pain, ulnar deviation, and swan-neck deformities. What is the diagnosis?
back:
- Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA).
- Key clinical hallmarks: Symmetric small joint involvement, ulnar deviation, and Boutonnière/Swan-neck deformities.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [They include ulnar deviation of the fingers, ‘swan neck’ deformity, the boutonnière or ‘buttonhole’ deformity and a Z deformity of the thumb.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: What is the initial pharmacological step for a patient newly diagnosed with Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back:
- Methotrexate (MTX) 15mg weekly.
- Co-prescription: Folic acid 5mg weekly.
- Escalation: Up to 25mg weekly based on response.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): [on first diagnosis... methotrexate (MTX) should be started in an initial dose of 15 mg weekly, along with folic acid 5 mg weekly, and escalated up to a maximum of 25 mg weekly.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: What total score is required on the ACR/EULAR 2010 criteria to classify a patient as having 'definite RA'?
back:
- Score ≥ 6.
- Components: Joint involvement, serology (RF/ACPA), acute phase reactants (CRP/ESR), and symptom duration.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Box 26.52: Patients with a score ≥ 6 are considered to have definite RA.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Differentiate RA from Psoriatic Arthritis (PsA) based on the involvement of the Distal Interphalangeal (DIP) joints.
back:
- RA: Typically spares the DIP joints.
- PsA: DIP involvement is a characteristic feature, often associated with nail dystrophy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1095 (Book Page): [Distal interphalangeal joint arthritis: This is quite a common pattern... in PsA psoriatic nail disease is usually present.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: How do you differentiate Chronic CPPD (Pseudogout) from RA in an elderly patient with Metacarpophalangeal (MCP) involvement?
back:
- CPPD: Targets 2nd and 3rd MCPs; spares 4th and 5th.
- RA: Symmetrical involvement of all MCP joints; ACPA positive.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1080 (Book Page): [Chronic CPP crystal arthritis can be mistaken for RA by the unwary, as MCP joints can be affected (usually just 2nd and 3rd, sparing the 4th and 5th) and low titre RF is a common incidental finding in old age.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Which systemic inflammatory mediator is responsible for triggering acute phase proteins in Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back:
- Interleukin-6 (IL-6).
- Action: Acts on the liver to produce CRP and serum amyloid A.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1027 (Book Page): [Systemic release of IL-6 triggers production of acute phase proteins by the liver.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: List the two specific types of hand nodes used to differentiate Nodal Osteoarthritis from RA.
back:
- Heberden’s nodes (DIP joints).
- Bouchard’s nodes (PIP joints).
- RA lacks these bony swellings and instead presents with soft-tissue synovitis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1074 (Book Page): [Gradually, these develop posterolateral swellings... which slowly enlarge and harden to become Heberden’s (DIP) and Bouchard’s (PIP) nodes.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
coreConcept: Clinical distinction of inflammatory vs degenerative stiffness.
front: How do Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) and Osteoarthritis (OA) differ regarding morning stiffness duration?
back:
• RA: Prolonged morning stiffness, typically lasting >1 hour.
• OA: Brief morning stiffness, typically lasting <15 minutes.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1074 (Book Page): [Typical OA pain has... Mild morning stiffness (< 15 mins)] and Page 1087 (Book Page): [typical presentation (RA) is with pain, joint swelling and stiffness... (early morning stiffness is severe)]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
coreConcept: Pannus-mediated erosion vs Mechanical cartilage degeneration.
front: Contrast the primary pathophysiological mechanism of joint destruction in RA versus OA.
back:
• RA: Inflammatory synovium (pannus) directly invades and erodes bone/cartilage.
• OA: Focal loss of articular cartilage with subchondral sclerosis and osteophyte formation.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1073 (Book Page): [Degeneration of articular cartilage is the defining feature of OA] and Page 1087 (Book Page): [inflamed synovium (pannus) directly invades bone and cartilage to cause joint erosions.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Which specific finger joints are involved in Nodal OA but typically spared in RA?
back:
• Distal Interphalangeal (DIP) joints (Heberden's nodes in OA).
• RA typically affects PIP and MCP joints while sparing the DIPs.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1074 (Book Page): [Heberden’s (DIP) and Bouchard’s (PIP) nodes] and Page 1087 (Book Page): [RA... small joints of the hands, feet and wrists in symmetrical fashion (DIP joints spared).]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
coreConcept: Differentiating RA from Pseudogout in the elderly.
front: An elderly patient presents with acute-onset polyarthritis and chondrocalcinosis on X-ray. What is the most likely diagnosis?
back:
• Chronic Calcium Pyrophosphate Deposition (CPPD) disease (Pseudogout).
• Key features: Elderly onset, knee/wrist involvement, and visible cartilage calcification.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1081 (Book Page): [Chronic CPP crystal arthritis can be mistaken for RA... affected joints usually show features of OA... X-rays may show evidence of calcification in hyaline cartilage.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
coreConcept: Early DMARD intervention to prevent erosions.
front: What is the mandatory pharmacological management goal upon confirming a diagnosis of RA?
back:
• Prompt initiation of conventional DMARDs (e.g., Methotrexate).
• Goal: Suppress inflammation and prevent permanent structural joint damage.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): [Prompt initiation of cDMARD therapy is indicated in all patients as this improves outcome... Methotrexate (MTX) should be started.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: List the four specific parameters used to calculate the Disease Activity Score (DAS28) in RA.
back:
1. Swollen joint count.
2. Tender joint count.
3. Inflammatory markers (ESR or CRP).
4. Patient global health assessment.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1091 (Book Page): [DAS28... involves counting the number of swollen and tender joints... combining this with the ESR and the patient’s assessment.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: How is joint involvement symmetry used to distinguish RA from Psoriatic Arthritis (PsA)?
back:
• RA: Characteristically symmetrical involvement.
• PsA: Typically asymmetrical oligoarthritis or ‘sausage digit’ (dactylitis).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [RA... small joints... in symmetrical fashion] and Page 1094 (Book Page): [Asymmetrical inflammatory mono-/oligoarthritis... sausage digit or dactylitis (PsA).]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Compare hand deformities in RA versus SLE regarding radiographic joint erosions.
back:
• RA: Deformities (Ulnar deviation) associated with marginal bone erosions.
• SLE: Deformities (Jaccoud’s arthropathy) are non-erosive and due to tendon damage.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1098 (Book Page): [Joint deformities may arise (Jaccoud’s arthropathy) as the result of tendon damage, but joint erosions are not a feature (of SLE).]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Differentiate the diagnostic utility of Rheumatoid Factor (RF) and ACPA for RA.
back:
• RF: Sensitive (70%) but less specific (found in infections/old age).
• ACPA: Highly specific (>95%) and identifies RA before clinical onset.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): [Tests for ACPA are positive in about 70% of cases and are highly specific for RA... RF is less specific than ACPA.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
coreConcept: Physical hallmarks of chronic Rheumatoid Arthritis.
front: Identify the classic 'Z-deformity' site and three common hand deformities in late RA.
back:
• Z-deformity: Affects the thumb.
• Hand: Ulnar deviation, Swan-neck, and Boutonnière deformities.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1088 (Book Page): [They include ulnar deviation of the fingers, ‘swan neck’ deformity, the boutonnière... and a Z deformity of the thumb.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Which specific joint group is typically spared in Rheumatoid Arthritis but commonly affected in Osteoarthritis?
back: The Distal Interphalangeal (DIP) joints.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [RA] typical presentation is with pain, joint swelling and stiffness affecting the small joints of the hands, feet and wrists in a symmetrical fashion. [Contrast with OA Page 1074 (Book Page): targeting the hips, knees, PIP and DIP joints].

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: What is the primary role of IL-6 in the systemic pathophysiology of Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: It triggers the liver to produce acute-phase proteins, such as C-reactive protein (CRP).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): Systemic release of IL-6 triggers production of acute phase proteins by the liver.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Differentiate the duration of morning stiffness in Rheumatoid Arthritis vs. Osteoarthritis.
back:
• RA: Severe and prolonged (>30–60 minutes).
• OA: Mild and brief (<15 minutes).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1074 (Book Page): [OA] Mild morning stiffness (< 15 mins) and inactivity gelling (< 5 mins). Page 1087 (Book Page): [RA] typical presentation is with... severe early morning stiffness.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: A patient presents with chronic symmetrical polyarthritis, high-titer RF, splenomegaly, and neutropenia. Diagnosis?
back: Felty Syndrome.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): Felty syndrome is a rare complication of seropositive RA in which splenomegaly occurs in combination with neutropenia and thrombocytopenia.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: What is the recommended first-line biologic class for RA failing conventional DMARDs?
back: Anti-TNF-α therapy (e.g., Infliximab, Etanercept).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1091 (Book Page): The most commonly used first-line biologic in RA is anti-TNF-α therapy, although several other options are available.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Which serological test is highly specific for RA and may predate clinical symptoms?
back: Anti-Citrullinated Peptide Antibody (ACPA).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): Tests for ACPA are positive in about 70% of cases and are highly specific for RA, occurring in many patients before clinical onset of the disease.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Contrast the pathological hallmark of RA with Osteoarthritis.
back:
• RA: Inflamed synovium (Pannus) directly invades/erodes bone and cartilage.
• OA: Focal loss of articular cartilage and subchondral sclerosis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): The inflamed synovium (pannus) directly invades bone and cartilage to cause joint erosions. Page 1073 (Book Page): [OA] characterized by focal loss of articular cartilage, subchondral osteosclerosis.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: How is Chronic CPPD (Pseudogout) differentiated from RA in an elderly patient with MCP involvement?
back:
• CPPD: Typically affects 2nd and 3rd MCP joints, sparing 4th and 5th.
• Imaging: Shows chondrocalcinosis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1080 (Book Page): Chronic CPP crystal arthritis can be mistaken for RA... as MCP joints can be affected (usually just 2nd and 3rd, sparing the 4th and 5th) and low titre RF is a common incidental finding in old age.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Describe the mechanism of bone erosion in Rheumatoid Arthritis involving the RANKL pathway.
back: Activated T-cells produce RANKL, which stimulates osteoclast activation and leads to periarticular bone erosion.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): A key pathogenic factor in bone erosions... is osteoclast activation, stimulated by the production of M-CSF by synovial cells and RANKL by activated T cells.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: List three characteristic hand deformities observed in long-standing Rheumatoid Arthritis.
back:
1. Ulnar deviation of fingers.
2. Swan-neck deformity.
3. Boutonnière deformity.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1088 (Book Page): They include ulnar deviation of the fingers, ‘swan neck’ deformity, the boutonnière or ‘buttonhole’ deformity and a Z deformity of the thumb.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: How does the duration of morning stiffness differentiate Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) from Osteoarthritis (OA)?
back: RA morning stiffness lasts >60 minutes, reflecting systemic inflammation. OA stiffness is transient, typically <15 minutes, with brief 'gelling' after rest.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1074 (Book Page): [OA Symptoms] Mild morning stiffness (< 15 mins) and inactivity gelling (< 5 mins) after rest.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Compare the distribution of hand joint involvement in Rheumatoid Arthritis versus Osteoarthritis.
back: RA targets MCP, PIP, and wrists (spares DIP). OA targets DIP (Heberden's) and PIP (Bouchard's) joints.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1074 (Book Page): [OA] targeting the hips, knees, PIP and DIP joints of the hands... [RA] small joints of the hands, feet and wrists in a symmetrical fashion.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Which laboratory marker is more specific for Rheumatoid Arthritis than Rheumatoid Factor (RF)?
back: Anti-citrullinated peptide antibodies (ACPA). While RF occurs in other diseases, ACPA is 70% positive and highly specific for RA.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): Tests for ACPA are positive in about 70% of cases and are highly specific for RA.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: A patient presents with symmetric polyarthritis and 'sausage-like' swelling of the fingers. Which feature differentiates this from RA?
back: Dactylitis ('sausage digit') and nail pitting indicate Psoriatic Arthritis (PsA), rather than Rheumatoid Arthritis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1095 (Book Page): [PsA] synovitis of a finger or toe is coupled with tenosynovitis... to give a ‘sausage digit’ or dactylitis.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: What is the mandatory pharmacological priority in RA compared to the symptomatic approach in OA?
back: Prompt initiation of cDMARDs (e.g., Methotrexate) to suppress inflammation and prevent damage. OA management prioritizes analgesia and lifestyle modifications.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): Prompt initiation of cDMARD therapy is indicated in all patients [with RA] as this improves outcome.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Under the 2010 ACR/EULAR criteria, what score confirms a definite diagnosis of Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: A total score of ≥ 6 out of 10, based on joint involvement, serology, symptom duration, and acute phase reactants.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): Patients with a score ≥ 6 are considered to have definite RA.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: How does CPPD (Pseudogout) involvement of the hand clinically contrast with typical RA involvement?
back: CPPD targets the 2nd and 3rd MCP joints (sparing 4th/5th) and exhibits chondrocalcinosis on X-ray, unlike the symmetric MCP involvement in RA.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1080 (Book Page): [Chronic CPPD] can be mistaken for RA... as MCP joints can be affected (usually just 2nd and 3rd, sparing the 4th and 5th).

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Describe the difference in visual appearance between tophi and rheumatoid nodules.
back: Tophi are white, chalky, and may ulcerate to discharge gritty material. Rheumatoid nodules are flesh-colored and usually subcutaneous.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1079 (Book Page): Tophi have a white colour, differentiating them from rheumatoid nodules. Tophi can ulcerate, discharging white gritty material.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: How do synovial fluid properties differ between an RA joint and an OA joint?
back: RA fluid is inflammatory (turbid, high neutrophils, low viscosity). OA fluid is non-inflammatory (clear, highly viscous, low cell count).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1076 (Book Page): Synovial fluid aspirated from an affected [OA] joint is viscous, with a low cell count.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Identify the defining radiographic hallmark of RA versus the hallmark of OA.
back: RA: Marginal joint erosions and periarticular osteoporosis. OA: Osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and joint space narrowing.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1073 (Book Page): [OA] is characterised by focal loss of articular cartilage, subchondral osteosclerosis, osteophyte formation.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: What are the characteristic joint distribution and primary laboratory markers used to diagnose Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back:
• Distribution: Symmetrical involvement of small joints (MCPs, PIPs, wrists, MTPs).
• Lab Markers: Rheumatoid Factor (RF) and Anti-Citrullinated Peptide Antibodies (ACPA).
• Inflammatory Markers: Elevated ESR and CRP.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [RA] typical presentation is with pain, joint swelling and stiffness affecting the small joints of the hands, feet and wrists in a symmetrical fashion... Tests for ACPA are positive in about 70% of cases and are highly specific for RA... RF is also positive in about 70%.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: How does the synovial pathology in Rheumatoid Arthritis differ fundamentally from the degenerative changes seen in Osteoarthritis?
back:
• RA: Autoimmune-driven pannus formation, inflammatory cell infiltration (T/B cells), and marginal bone erosions.
• OA: Focal loss of articular cartilage, subchondral sclerosis, and marginal osteophyte (bony) formation.
• Inflammation: Marked in RA; mild or absent in OA.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): The disease is characterised by infiltration of synovium with lymphocytes... the inflamed synovium (pannus) directly invades bone and cartilage to cause joint erosions. Page 1073 (Book Page): Osteoarthritis... characterised by focal loss of articular cartilage, subchondral osteosclerosis, osteophyte formation.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Differentiate Rheumatoid Arthritis from Psoriatic Arthritis and Gout based on specific clinical findings and X-ray features.
back:
• RA: Symmetrical small joint involvement; marginal erosions; spares DIP joints.
• PsA: Dactylitis (sausage digit); nail pitting; involves DIP joints; asymmetric.
• Gout: Podagra (1st MTP); punched-out erosions; needle-shaped urate crystals.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1096 (Book Page): [PsA] synovitis of a finger or toe is coupled with tenosynovitis... to give a ‘sausage digit’ or dactylitis... distal interphalangeal joint arthritis... is quite a common pattern. Page 1080 (Book Page): [Gout] well-demarcated erosions may be seen in patients with chronic or tophaceous gout.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: What is the most specific laboratory marker for Rheumatoid Arthritis diagnosis?
back: Anti-citrullinated peptide antibody (ACPA). It is positive in ~70% of cases and is highly specific for RA, often preceding clinical onset.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Tests for ACPA are positive in about 70% of cases and are highly specific for RA, occurring in many patients before clinical onset of the disease.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Describe the pathophysiological mechanism of bone erosion in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
back: Mediated by osteoclast activation. Synovial cells produce M-CSF and activated T cells produce RANKL, stimulating osteoclasts to invade bone at the joint margin (pannus).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1086 (Book Page): [A key pathogenic factor in bone erosions and periarticular osteoporosis is osteoclast activation, stimulated by the production of M-CSF by synovial cells and RANKL by activated T cells.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Differentiate the morning stiffness of RA from Osteoarthritis (OA).
back: RA: Severe, lasting >60 minutes. OA: Mild, lasting <15 minutes. OA also features 'inactivity gelling' lasting <5 minutes.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1074 (Book Page): [Typical OA pain has the characteristics: Mild morning stiffness (< 15 mins) and inactivity gelling (< 5 mins) after rest.] Page 1086 (Book Page): [The typical presentation is with pain, joint swelling and stiffness... in a symmetrical fashion.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: A patient with RA presents with acute calf pain and swelling mimicking DVT. Name the likely complication.
back: Ruptured Popliteal (Baker's) cyst. Caused by synovial fluid communication with the cyst via a valve-like mechanism under pressure.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Popliteal (Baker’s) cysts may occur in patients with knee synovitis... Rupture may be induced by knee flexion, leading to calf pain and swelling that may mimic a deep venous thrombosis.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: What is the standard first-line pharmacological treatment algorithm for newly diagnosed RA?
back: Prompt initiation of cDMARDs, typically Methotrexate (15mg weekly) combined with short-term bridging glucocorticoids (e.g., Prednisolone 30mg daily tapering over 12 weeks).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): [On first diagnosis, prednisolone can be started in a dose of 30 mg daily gradually reducing... methotrexate (MTX) should be started in an initial dose of 15 mg weekly.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: List the four clinical/laboratory domains used in the ACR/EULAR 2010 criteria for RA classification.
back: 1. Joint involvement. 2. Serology (RF/ACPA). 3. Duration of symptoms (>6 weeks). 4. Acute-phase reactants (CRP/ESR).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Criteria for diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis: Joints affected, Serology, Duration of symptoms, Acute phase reactants.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Which hand joint involvement distinguishes Psoriatic Arthritis from typical Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: Distal interphalangeal (DIP) joints. RA typically spares the DIPs, whereas DIP involvement with nail dystrophy is characteristic of PsA.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1095 (Book Page): [Distal interphalangeal joint arthritis: This is quite a common pattern. It can be difficult to distinguish from inflammatory generalised OA, but in PsA psoriatic nail disease is usually present.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: An elderly patient presents with RA-like symmetrical polyarthritis but is RF-negative and has chondrocalcinosis. Diagnosis?
back: Chronic CPP crystal arthritis (Pseudogout). It can involve the 2nd and 3rd MCP joints and mimic RA in older populations.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1080 (Book Page): [Chronic CPP crystal arthritis can be mistaken for RA by the unwary, as MCP joints can be affected (usually just 2nd and 3rd, sparing the 4th and 5th) and low titre RF is a common incidental finding in old age.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Which cytokine is primarily responsible for the hepatic acute-phase response (elevated CRP) in RA?
back: Interleukin-6 (IL-6). It is produced by macrophages and fibroblasts and acts systemically on the liver to produce acute-phase proteins.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1086 (Book Page): [Systemic release of IL-6 triggers production of acute phase proteins by the liver.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Define the clinical triad of Felty Syndrome occurring in chronic RA.
back: 1. Rheumatoid Arthritis (usually long-standing/seropositive). 2. Splenomegaly. 3. Neutropenia.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): [Felty syndrome is a rare complication of seropositive RA in which splenomegaly occurs in combination with neutropenia and thrombocytopenia.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Which laboratory markers are most specific for diagnosing Rheumatoid Arthritis in patients with polyarthritis?
back: Anti-citrullinated peptide antibodies (ACPA) and Rheumatoid Factor (RF). ACPA is highly specific (70%) and often precedes clinical onset.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): [Tests for ACPA are positive in about 70% of cases and are highly specific for RA, occurring in many patients before clinical onset of the disease.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: What is the primary pathological joint feature differentiating RA from Osteoarthritis?
back: RA: Chronic synovial inflammation (synovitis) and pannus invading bone. OA: Focal loss of articular cartilage and subchondral sclerosis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [The inflamed synovium (pannus) directly invades bone and cartilage to cause joint erosions... Degeneration of articular cartilage is the defining feature of OA.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: How does the duration of morning stiffness differentiate RA from Osteoarthritis clinical findings?
back: RA: Prolonged morning stiffness (>1 hour). OA: Brief morning stiffness (<15-30 minutes) and 'gelling' after inactivity.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1074 (Book Page): [Mild morning stiffness (< 15 mins) and inactivity gelling (< 5 mins) after rest... typical OA pain.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: A patient presents with dactylitis and DIP joint involvement. Which condition is most likely over RA?
back: Psoriatic Arthritis (PsA). RA typically spares distal interphalangeal (DIP) joints and does not cause 'sausage digits' (dactylitis).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1096 (Book Page): [synovitis of a finger or toe is coupled with tenosynovitis... to give a ‘sausage digit’ or dactylitis... DIP joint arthritis is quite a common pattern.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: What is the initial pharmacological step in managing a new diagnosis of Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: Start Methotrexate (MTX) weekly, often with folic acid. Short-term bridging prednisolone is used to suppress immediate inflammation.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1091 (Book Page): [On first diagnosis, prednisolone can be started... At the same time, methotrexate (MTX) should be started in an initial dose of 15 mg weekly.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Which scoring system monitors RA disease activity using swollen/tender joint counts and inflammatory markers?
back: DAS28 (Disease Activity Score in 28 joints). It categorizes RA activity into Remission, Low, Moderate, or High.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): [The Disease Activity Score in 28 joints (DAS28) is widely used to assess disease activity, response to treatment and need for biologic therapy.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: How do Jaccoud's arthropathy in SLE and joint findings in RA compare radiologically?
back: SLE: Deformities are due to tendon laxity and are non-erosive. RA: Characterized by marginal joint erosions on X-ray.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1098 (Book Page): [Joint deformities may arise (Jaccoud’s arthropathy) as the result of tendon damage, but joint erosions are not a feature [in SLE].]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: A patient with suspected gout has normal serum uric acid during an attack. Diagnosis?
back: Still Gout. Serum urate often falls during acute flares; identification of monosodium urate crystals in synovial fluid is diagnostic.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1080 (Book Page): [Hyperuricaemia is usually present... but levels may be normal during an attack because serum urate falls during inflammation.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: What metabolic enzyme is the target of the first-line urate-lowering therapy Allopurinol?
back: Xanthine Oxidase. It catalyzes the conversion of hypoxanthine and xanthine into uric acid.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1079 (Book Page): [xanthine oxidase plays a pivotal role in catalysing the conversion of hypoxanthine to xanthine and xanthine to uric acid.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: What are the characteristic bony swellings of DIP and PIP joints in Osteoarthritis called?
back: Heberden’s nodes (DIP) and Bouchard’s nodes (PIP). These represent bony osteophytes, differentiating them from RA soft-tissue swelling.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1074 (Book Page): [develop posterolateral swellings... which slowly enlarge and harden to become Heberden’s (DIP) and Bouchard’s (PIP) nodes.]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What are the four hallmark radiographic features of Osteoarthritis (OA)?
back:
• Focal loss of articular cartilage (joint space narrowing)
• Subchondral osteosclerosis
• Osteophyte formation at joint margins
• Subchondral cysts
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1073 (Book Page): [Osteoarthritis] is characterised by focal loss of articular cartilage, subchondral osteosclerosis, osteophyte formation at the joint margin and remodelling of joint contour with enlargement of affected joints... subchondral bone, which becomes sclerotic and the site of subchondral cysts.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Which investigation is the gold standard for confirming a diagnosis of Gout?
back:
• Identification of monosodium urate crystals in joint aspirate
• Observed via compensated polarised microscopy
• Characterized as needle-shaped with negative birefringence
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1079 (Book Page): The diagnosis of gout can be confirmed by the identification of urate crystals in the aspirate from a joint, bursa or tophus... Fig. 26.6A [shows needle-shaped negative birefringence].

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: How do Calcium Pyrophosphate (CPP) crystals differ from Gout crystals under polarised microscopy?
back:
• CPP: Rhomboid or rod-shaped; weakly positive birefringence
• Gout: Needle-shaped; strongly negative birefringence
