citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1081 (Book Page): demonstrate CPP crystals... [Fig 26.6B shows rhomboid/rod shape, positive birefringence vs Gout's needle/negative].

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: In a patient with suspected septic arthritis, which investigation is the most urgent 'pivotal' step?
back:
• Immediate joint aspiration
• Urgent Gram stain and culture
• Mandatory blood cultures to identify haematogenous spread
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1084 (Book Page): The pivotal investigation is joint aspiration, but blood cultures should also be taken. The synovial fluid should be sent for Gram stain and culture.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Which serum autoantibody is most specific for Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) diagnosis?
back:
• Anti-citrullinated peptide antibody (ACPA)
• Note: Rheumatoid Factor (RF) is common but less specific
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): Tests for ACPA are positive in about 70% of cases and are highly specific for RA... RF is less specific than ACPA.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What are the primary diagnostic indicators used to calculate the DAS28 score in RA?
back:
• Number of swollen joints
• Number of tender joints
• ESR or C-reactive protein (CRP)
• Patient global health visual analogue scale
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): It involves counting the number of swollen and tender joints... combining this with the ESR and the patient’s assessment of the activity of their arthritis on a visual analogue scale.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Which biochemical markers indicate active complement consumption during an SLE flare?
back:
• Low serum C3 levels
• Low serum C4 levels
• Elevated anti-dsDNA antibody titers
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1099 (Book Page): Serum levels of C3 may be low in active SLE due to complement consumption... Anti-dsDNA antibodies are positive in most patients and are quite specific for SLE.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Which autoantibody differentiates Diffuse Systemic Sclerosis (dcSScl) from the Limited form (lcSScl)?
back:
• dcSScl: Anti-topoisomerase 1 (Scl70) antibodies
• lcSScl: Anti-centromere antibodies
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1100 (Book Page): About 30% of patients with dcSScl have antibodies to topoisomerase 1 (Scl70). About 60% of patients [with lcSScl] have anticentromere antibodies.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What findings on a muscle biopsy confirm a diagnosis of Polymyositis?
back:
• Muscle fiber necrosis
• Evidence of fiber regeneration
• Significant inflammatory cell infiltrate
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1102 (Book Page): Muscle biopsy is the pivotal investigation and shows the typical features of fibre necrosis, regeneration and inflammatory cell infiltrate.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What is the gold standard investigation for diagnosing Giant Cell Arteritis (GCA)?
back:
• Temporal artery biopsy
• Alternative: Doppler ultrasound (showing the 'halo sign')
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1105 (Book Page): The two most commonly used investigations are temporal artery biopsy and ultrasound... typical biopsy findings are fragmentation of the internal elastic lamina... ultrasound... is the ‘halo’ sign.

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
coreConcept: Joint Distribution in RA vs OA
front: Q: Which specific small joints are typically involved in RA compared to Osteoarthritis (OA)?
back: RA targets MCP and PIP joints symmetrically while sparing the DIPs. OA targets DIP joints (Heberden's nodes) and the first CMC joint.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1074 (Book Page): [Osteoarthritis has a characteristic distribution, mainly targeting the hips, knees, PIP and DIP joints] Page 1087 (Book Page): [The typical presentation is with pain, joint swelling and stiffness affecting the small joints of the hands, feet and wrists in a symmetrical fashion.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: How does the duration of morning stiffness differentiate RA from mechanical Osteoarthritis?
back: RA stiffness is prolonged, lasting >60 minutes. OA stiffness is brief, usually <15-30 minutes, often called 'inactivity gelling'.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1074 (Book Page): [Mild morning stiffness (< 15 mins) and inactivity gelling (< 5 mins) after rest] Page 1087 (Book Page): [RA has an acute onset, with severe early morning stiffness...]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Differentiate RA from Psoriatic Arthritis (PsA) based on joint pattern and digit appearance.
back: RA is symmetric and lacks dactylitis. PsA is often asymmetric, involves DIP joints, and presents with 'sausage digits' (dactylitis) and nail pitting.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1095 (Book Page): [synovitis of a finger or toe is coupled with tenosynovitis... to give a ‘sausage digit’ or dactylitis... psoriatic nail disease is usually present]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: In an elderly patient with MCP involvement, how is RA distinguished from Chronic CPP Arthritis?
back: RA is ACPA positive with marginal erosions. Chronic CPP (Pseudogout) shows chondrocalcinosis on X-ray and spares the 4th/5th MCP joints.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1080 (Book Page): [Chronic CPP crystal arthritis can be mistaken for RA by the unwary, as MCP joints can be affected (usually just 2nd and 3rd, sparing the 4th and 5th)]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Which laboratory markers differentiate SLE-related polyarthritis from Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: RA shows positive ACPA/RF and erosions. SLE shows ANA/anti-dsDNA positivity, low complement (C3/C4), and non-erosive arthritis (Jaccoud’s).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1098 (Book Page): [Joint deformities may arise (Jaccoud’s arthropathy)... but joint erosions are not a feature... active SLE are almost always positive for ANA.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: According to the 2010 ACR/EULAR criteria, what score is diagnostic for definite RA?
back: A total score of 6 or more out of 10 points is required to confirm definite RA.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Patients with a score >= 6 are considered to have definite RA.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Differentiate RA from Adult-onset Still’s Disease based on specific laboratory findings.
back: RA is RF/ACPA positive. Still’s is RF/ACPA negative and presents with markedly elevated serum ferritin and a salmon-pink rash.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1104 (Book Page): [Adult-onset Still’s disease... typical laboratory abnormalities... markedly elevated serum ferritin. Tests for RF and ANA are negative.]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: How does a ruptured Baker's cyst in RA mimic a DVT clinically?
back: Both present with sudden calf pain and swelling. RA history and ultrasound evidence of synovial communication confirm a ruptured popliteal cyst.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Rupture may be induced by knee flexion, leading to calf pain and swelling that may mimic a deep venous thrombosis (DVT).]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: How does synovial fluid analysis distinguish RA from Gouty polyarthritis?
back: RA fluid is inflammatory without crystals. Gout is confirmed by identifying needle-shaped, negatively birefringent monosodium urate crystals.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1079 (Book Page): [The diagnosis of gout can be confirmed by the identification of urate crystals in the aspirate from a joint...]

category: Differentiate RA from other causes of polyarthritis based on clinical and laboratory findings
front: Q: Why is ACPA testing preferred over Rheumatoid Factor (RF) for RA diagnosis?
back: ACPA is highly specific (approx. 98%) and often appears years before clinical onset, whereas RF is less specific and occurs in other diseases.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): [Tests for ACPA are positive in about 70% of cases and are highly specific for RA... RF is less specific than ACPA]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What are the four cardinal radiological features of osteoarthritis visible on a plain joint X-ray?
back:
1. Joint space narrowing
2. Subchondral sclerosis
3. Osteophyte formation at joint margins
4. Subchondral cysts
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1073 (Book Page): [Osteoarthritis] is characterised by focal loss of articular cartilage, subchondral osteosclerosis, osteophyte formation at the joint margin and remodelling of joint contour... subchondral bone, which becomes sclerotic and the site of subchondral cysts.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Which serological investigation is highly specific for Rheumatoid Arthritis and can predate clinical disease onset?
back:
• Anti-citrullinated peptide antibody (ACPA).
• Positive in ~70% of cases.
• Higher specificity for RA than Rheumatoid Factor (RF).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): Tests for ACPA are positive in about 70% of cases and are highly specific for RA, occurring in many patients before clinical onset of the disease.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Contrast the typical ANCA serology findings in Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (GPA) versus Microscopic Polyangiitis (MPA).
back:
• GPA: Proteinase-3 (PR3) antibody positive.
• MPA: Myeloperoxidase (MPO) antibody positive.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1104 (Book Page): Patients with GPA are usually proteinase-3 (PR3) antibody-positive... Patients [with MPA] are usually myeloperoxidase (MPO) antibody-positive.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: A patient has inflammatory back pain but normal spinal X-rays. What pivotal investigation confirms axial spondyloarthritis?
back:
• MRI of the sacroiliac joints.
• It detects active inflammation (bone marrow oedema/osteitis) before structural changes appear on X-ray.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1093 (Book Page): Inflammatory changes in the axial skeleton (such as sacroiliitis...) are characteristic of axSpA and are visualised by MRI. Radiological alterations... develop later in the course of the disease.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What is the gold standard investigation for diagnosing gout, and what does it demonstrate?
back:
• Joint aspiration and Compensated Polarized Microscopy.
• Demonstrates needle-shaped, negatively birefringent monosodium urate crystals.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1079 (Book Page): The diagnosis of gout can be confirmed by the identification of urate crystals in the aspirate from a joint, bursa or tophus.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Which biochemical marker is characteristically markedly elevated in Adult-onset Still’s disease during investigations?
back:
• Serum Ferritin.
• Often extremely high in conjunction with a neutrophilia and raised ESR/CRP.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1104 (Book Page): Investigations typically provide evidence of an acute phase response with raised ESR and CRP and a markedly elevated serum ferritin.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Why is MRI preferred over plain X-ray in the investigation of suspected spinal tuberculosis (Pott’s disease)?
back:
• MRI is more sensitive for early disease.
• Better visualizes bone destruction, disc narrowing, and encroaching soft tissue masses/abscesses.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): Imaging with MRI is more sensitive than X-rays at detecting the features of osteoarticular TB and is the imaging investigation of first choice.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
coreConcept: ANA and Uveitis risk in JIA
front: Q: In Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (JIA), what does a positive Antinuclear Antibody (ANA) test signify regarding prognosis?
back:
• Indicates a significantly increased risk of chronic uveitis.
• Mandates regular ophthalmic screening with a slit-lamp.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1092 (Book Page): A positive ANA occurs in 40%–75% of cases of JIA and indicates an increased risk of eye disease.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What are the primary laboratory findings in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) reflecting active disease?
back:
• Raised ESR with normal/low CRP.
• Low complement (C3/C4) levels.
• Leucopenia, lymphopenia, or thrombocytopenia.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1100 (Book Page): CRP is often normal in active SLE... Serum levels of C3 may be low in active SLE due to complement consumption. A raised ESR, leucopenia and lymphopenia are typical.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What is the pivotal investigation for confirming a diagnosis of polymyositis?
back:
• Muscle Biopsy.
• Findings: Muscle fibre necrosis, regeneration, and inflammatory cell infiltrate.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1103 (Book Page): Muscle biopsy is the pivotal investigation and shows the typical features of fibre necrosis, regeneration and inflammatory cell infiltrate.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What is the definitive investigation for confirming a diagnosis of gout?
back:
• Identification of monosodium urate crystals in joint aspirate, bursa, or tophus.
• Viewed via compensated polarized light microscopy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1079 (Book Page): [The diagnosis of gout can be conrmed by the identication of urate crystals in the aspirate fr om a joint, bursa or tophus]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Why do serum complement levels (C3/C4) fall during active SLE flare?
back:
• Complement consumption occurs due to immune complex formation and subsequent tissue damage.
• Low levels correlate with increased disease activity.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1099 (Book Page): [Serum levels of C3 may be low in active SLE due to complement consumption]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Contrast the specificity of Rheumatoid Factor (RF) versus ACPA in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
back:
• RF: Positive in 70% but less specific; can occur in other diseases.
• ACPA: Highly specific for RA (70% positive); often appears before clinical onset.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): [T ests for ACP A ar e positive in about 70% of cases and ar e highly specic for RA... RF is less specic than ACP A]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: In a patient with suspected CPPD, why is Gram stain of synovial fluid mandatory?
back:
• Sepsis and acute CPP crystal arthritis (pseudogout) can coexist.
• Must exclude septic arthritis even if crystals are present.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1081 (Book Page): [Since sepsis and acute CPP crys - tal arthritis can coexist, Gram stain and cultur e of the uid should be performed to exclude sepsis, even if CPP crystals ar e identied]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Which baseline investigations are required to monitor drug safety in patients starting DMARDs?
back:
• Full Blood Count (FBC).
• Liver Function Tests (LFTs).
• Urea and Creatinine.
• Urinalysis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): [T o monitor drug safety: Urinalysis, Urea and creatinine, Full blood count, Liver function tests]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Name the four components of the DAS28 score used in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
back:
1. Swollen joint count.
2. Tender joint count.
3. Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR) or CRP.
4. Patient global health assessment.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): [Calculation: Count swollen joints, Count tender joints, Measur e erythr ocyte sedimentation rate, Note patient global health assessment]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What specific radiographic views are required for diagnosing suspected Knee Osteoarthritis?
back:
• Standing Anteroposterior (AP) view (to assess tibio-femoral cartilage loss).
• Flexed skyline view (to assess patello-femoral involvement).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1076 (Book Page): [Patients with suspected knee OA should have standing anter oposterior X-rays taken... and a exed skyline view to assess patello-femoral involvement]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Differentiate the autoantibody profiles of Limited versus Diffuse Systemic Sclerosis.
back:
• Diffuse (dcSScl): Anti-topoisomerase 1 (Scl70) antibodies.
• Limited (lcSScl/CREST): Anti-centromere antibodies.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1100 (Book Page): [About 30% of patients with dcSScl have antibodies to topoisomer - ase 1 (Scl70). About 60% of patients have anticentr omer e antibodies and this is a biomarker for lcSScl]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Which biochemical tests are necessary for Gout patients due to its association with Metabolic Syndrome?
back:
• Renal function tests.
• Serum Uric Acid (SUA).
• Fasting Glucose.
• Lipid profile.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1079 (Book Page): [A biochemical scr een, including r enal function, uric acid, glucose and lipid pr ole, should be performed because of the association with met - abolic syndr ome]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What is the pivotal investigation for diagnosing Polymyositis or Dermatomyositis?
back:
• Muscle Biopsy.
• Typical findings: Fiber necrosis, regeneration, and inflammatory cell infiltrate.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1103 (Book Page): [Muscle b i o p s y i s t h e p i v o t a l i n v e s t i g a t i o n a n d s h o w s t h e t y p i c a l f e a - t u r e s o f  b r e n e c r o s i s , r e g e n e r a t i o n a n d i n  a m m a t o r y c e l l i n  l t r a t e]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
coreConcept: Definitive Diagnostic Gold Standard for Gout
front: Q: What is the definitive investigation to confirm a diagnosis of Gout?
back:
- Identification of monosodium urate monohydrate crystals in synovial fluid
- Crystals appear needle-shaped and negatively birefringent under polarized microscopy
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1079 (Book Page): [The diagnosis of gout can be conﬁrmed by the identiﬁcation of urate crystals in the aspirate fr om a joint, bursa or tophus.]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Name the four hallmark radiological features of Osteoarthritis (OA) seen on a plain X-ray.
back:
1. Focal loss of articular joint space
2. Subchondral osteosclerosis
3. Osteophyte formation at joint margins
4. Subchondral cysts
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1073 (Book Page): [It is characterised by focal loss of articular cartilage, subchondral osteoscler osis, osteophyte formation at the joint margin and r emodelling of joint contour with enlargement of af fected joints.]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Contrast the appearance of Gout vs. CPPD (Pseudogout) crystals under compensated polarized light.
back:
- Gout: Needle-shaped; strongly negative birefringence
- CPPD: Rhomboid/brick-shaped; weakly positive birefringence
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1081 (Book Page): [demonstrate CPP crystals (see Fig. 26.6B). ... In acute gout, the synovial ﬂuid may be turbid ...identiﬁcation of urate crystals (see Fig. 26.6A).]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: In a patient with an acute hot joint, which investigation is mandatory even if crystals are visualized?
back:
- Synovial fluid Gram stain and Culture
- Mandatory to exclude coexisting septic arthritis which is rapidly destructive
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1082 (Book Page): [Since sepsis and acute CPP crystal arthritis can coexist, Gram stain and cultur e of the ﬂuid should be performed to exclude sepsis, even if CPP crystals ar e identiﬁed.]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Which autoantibody has the highest specificity for Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) diagnosis?
back:
- Anti-citrullinated peptide antibody (ACPA / Anti-CCP)
- Found in ~70% of cases; more specific than Rheumatoid Factor (RF)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): [T ests for ACP A ar e positive in about 70% of cases and ar e highly speciﬁc for RA... RF is less speciﬁc than ACP A.]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What is the specific biomarker for monitoring disease activity and renal involvement in SLE?
back:
- Anti-double-stranded DNA (anti-dsDNA) antibodies
- Serum Complement levels (C3/C4); levels fall during active flares due to consumption
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1099 (Book Page): [Anti-dsDNA antibodies ar e positive in most patients and ar e quite speciﬁc for SLE. Serum levels of C3 may be low in active SLE due to complement consumption.]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What imaging modality is most sensitive for detecting early sacroiliitis in Axial Spondyloarthritis?
back:
- MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging)
- Detects bone marrow oedema/osteitis before radiographic changes appear on X-ray
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1092 (Book Page): [Inﬂammatory changes in the axial skeleton (such as sacr oiliitis, see Fig. 26.40) ar e characteristic of axSpA and ar e visualised by MRI.]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: In Systemic Sclerosis (Scleroderma), which autoantibody is associated with diffuse disease and lung fibrosis?
back:
- Anti-topoisomerase 1 (Anti-Scl70) antibody
- Associated with diffuse cutaneous involvement and interstitial lung disease
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1100 (Book Page): [About 30% of patients with dcSScl have antibodies to topoisomer ase 1 (Scl70). ...a biomarker for lcSScl and CREST syndr ome.]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: A child with Oligoarticular JIA tests ANA positive. Which specialty investigation is required urgently?
back:
- Slit-lamp ophthalmic screening
- Positive ANA indicates a high risk for asymptomatic, chronic anterior uveitis
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1091 (Book Page): [A positive ANA occurs in 40%–75% of cases of JIA and indicates an incr eased risk of eye disease.]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What is the significance of the 'Halo Sign' on temporal artery ultrasound?
back:
- Indicates Giant Cell Arteritis (GCA)
- Represents vessel wall thickening/oedema surrrounding the arterial lumen
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1105 (Book Page): [The characteristic ﬁnding on Doppler ultrasound examination is the ‘halo’ sign, wher e the thickened vessel wall shows as a dark ar ea surr ounding a positive Doppler signal.]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What are the four characteristic radiological features of Osteoarthritis visible on a plain X-ray?
back: 1. Focal loss of articular cartilage (asymmetric joint space narrowing). 2. Subchondral osteosclerosis (increased bone density). 3. Osteophyte formation at joint margins. 4. Subchondral cyst formation.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1073 (Book Page): "[Osteoarthritis] is characterised by focal loss of articular cartilage, subchondral osteoscler osis, osteo-phyte formation at the joint margin and r emodelling of joint contour with enlargement of af fected joints."

category: Interpret relevant investigations
coreConcept: Interpretation of Serum Urate in Acute Gout
front: Q: Why is a normal serum uric acid level insufficient to rule out an acute gouty attack?
back: Serum urate levels may fall into the normal range during an acute flare because systemic inflammation decreases circulating urate. Definitive diagnosis requires identifying monosodium urate crystals in synovial fluid aspirate.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1080 (Book Page): "Hyperuricaemia is usually pr esent in gout, but levels may be normal during an attack because serum urate falls during inammation."

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Contrast the appearance of Gout and Pseudogout (CPPD) crystals under compensated polarized microscopy.
back: Gout: Needle-shaped Monosodium Urate crystals with strong negative birefringence. Pseudogout (CPPD): Rhomboid or brick-shaped Calcium Pyrophosphate crystals with weak positive birefringence.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1082 (Book Page): "The pivotal investigation in diagnosing acute CPP crystal arthritis is joint aspiration, followed by examination of synovial uid using compensated polarised micr oscopy to demonstrate CPP crystals."

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Which international classification criteria are currently the gold standard for confirming Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: The ACR/EULAR 2010 Classification Criteria for RA.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Clinical criteria for the diagnosis of RA are shown in Box 26.52... European League Against Rheumatism/American College of Rheumatology 2010 criteria.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: How does the process of citrullination contribute to the diagnostic serology used in RA?
back: Environmental triggers (smoking) modify host proteins via citrullination; these become immunogenic, triggering the production of diagnostic anti-citrullinated peptide antibodies (ACPA).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [RA occurs when an environmental stimulus... triggers autoimmunity... by modifying host proteins, through processes like citrullination, so that they become immunogenic... causing activation of B cells to produce... ACPA.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Between Rheumatoid Factor (RF) and ACPA, which marker is more specific for confirming RA and why?
back: ACPA; it is highly specific and can appear before clinical symptom onset, whereas RF is found in other diseases.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): [Tests for ACPA are positive in about 70% of cases and are highly specific for RA... RF is less specific than ACPA, however, and positive tests can occur in other diseases.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Apply 2010 criteria: A patient has 11 involved small joints for 8 weeks and raised CRP. Does this confirm RA?
back: Yes. Score = 7 total. (>10 joints = 5; Duration >6 weeks = 1; Raised CRP = 1). Score ≥6 is diagnostic.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Box 26.52: > 10 joints (at least 1 small joint) 5; > 6 weeks 1; Abnormal CRP or ESR 1. Patients with a score ≥ 6 are considered to have definite RA.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: What are the four essential clinical parameters required to calculate a DAS28 score?
back:
1. Swollen joint count
2. Tender joint count
3. ESR or CRP level
4. Patient global health (Visual Analogue Scale).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): [Fig. 26.37: Count swollen joints; Count tender joints; Measure erythrocyte sedimentation rate; Note patient global health assessment (1–100).]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: According to ACR/EULAR 2010, what is the minimum score required to classify a patient as having 'definite RA'?
back: A total score of 6 or higher.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Patients with a score ≥ 6 are considered to have definite RA.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: In the ACR/EULAR 2010 criteria, what is the significance of 'small joint' involvement versus 'large joint'?
back: Small joint involvement yields higher points (2–5) compared to large joints (0–1), reflecting RA's characteristic targeting of small joints.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Box 26.52: 1 large joint 0; 2–10 large joints 1; 1–3 small joints 2; 4–10 small joints 3; > 10 joints (at least 1 small joint) 5.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: A 70-year-old presents with acute morning stiffness and pitting edema. Which RA variant does this suggest?
back: Acute-onset RA, which commonly occurs in old age and may mimic polymyalgia rheumatica.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Sometimes RA has an acute onset, with severe early morning stiffness, polyarthritis and pitting oedema. This occurs more commonly in old age.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Which specific cytokine systemically triggers the hepatic production of CRP used in RA diagnostics?
back: Interleukin-6 (IL-6).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Systemic release of IL-6 triggers production of acute phase proteins by the liver.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Define the typical clinical joint distribution used to identify Rheumatoid Arthritis at presentation.
back: Symmetrical involvement of small joints of the hands, feet, and wrists.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [The typical presentation is with pain, joint swelling and stiffness affecting the small joints of the hands, feet and wrists in a symmetrical fashion.]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What is the gold standard investigation for confirming a diagnosis of Gout?
back: Identification of monosodium urate crystals in synovial fluid aspirate (from joint, bursa, or tophus) using polarized microscopy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1079 (Book Page): [The diagnosis of gout can be confirmed by the identification of urate crystals in the aspirate from a joint, bursa or tophus]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: How is polarized microscopy used to differentiate CPPD (Pseudogout) from Gout?
back:
• CPPD: Positively birefringent, rhomboid-shaped calcium pyrophosphate crystals.
• Gout: Negatively birefringent, needle-shaped monosodium urate crystals.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1081 (Book Page): [diagnosing acute CPP crystal arthritis is joint aspiration, followed by examination of synovial fluid using compensated polarised microscopy to demonstrate CPP crystals]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Contrast the radiological features of Osteoarthritis (OA) and Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA).
back:
• OA: Joint space narrowing, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and cysts.
• RA: Marginal erosions and periarticular osteoporosis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): [periarticular osteoporosis and marginal joint erosions may be observed with more advanced disease (RA)]; Page 1073 (Book Page): [OA... characterised by focal loss of articular cartilage, subchondral osteosclerosis, osteophyte formation]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: In a suspected SLE flare, how are Complement C3/C4 and CRP levels interpreted?
back:
• Complement (C3/C4): Low levels (due to consumption during active disease).
• CRP: Typically normal in SLE flares (elevation suggests infection or serositis).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1099 (Book Page): [Serum levels of C3 may be low in active SLE due to complement consumption... CRP is often normal in active SLE]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What is the diagnostic significance of nail-fold capillaroscopy in systemic sclerosis?
back: It differentiates primary Raynaud’s from secondary (SScl) by showing capillary loop loss (fallout), dilatation, and branching.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1098 (Book Page): [Examination of capillary nail-fold loops... can show loss of the normal loop pattern, with capillary ‘fallout’ and dilatation and branching of loops; these features support a diagnosis of secondary RP]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Name the four clinical/laboratory components used to calculate the RA DAS28 score.
back:
1. Swollen joint count.
2. Tender joint count.
3. Inflammatory markers (ESR or CRP).
4. Patient global health assessment (VAS).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): [swollen and tender joints... combining this with the ESR and the patient’s assessment of the activity of their arthritis on a visual analogue scale]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Why is MRI preferred over plain X-ray in suspected early-stage Osteomyelitis?
back: MRI is significantly more sensitive for detecting marrow edema and early inflammatory changes before bony destruction is visible on X-ray.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1085 (Book Page): [Patients suspected of having osteomyelitis should have an MRI, which is more sensitive than X-ray for detecting early changes.]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: How does a muscle biopsy differentiate active Polymyositis from Glucocorticoid-induced myopathy?
back:
• Active Myositis: Shows fiber necrosis, regeneration, and inflammatory infiltrates.
• Glucocorticoid Myopathy: Shows Type II fiber atrophy without inflammatory cells.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1102 (Book Page): [case of glucocorticoid myopathy type II fibre atrophy is observed as compared with fibre necrosis and regeneration in active myositis.]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Which specific antibodies are associated with Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (GPA)?
back: Proteinase-3 (PR3) antibodies, typically presenting as a c-ANCA (cytoplasmic) pattern on immunofluorescence.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1103 (Book Page): [Patients with GPA are usually proteinase-3 (PR3) antibody-positive.]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What are the characteristic findings in Synovial Fluid analysis for Osteoarthritis?
back: The fluid is highly viscous with a low total cell count (non-inflammatory).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1076 (Book Page): [Synovial fluid aspirated from an affected joint is viscous, with a low cell count.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: According to 2010 EULAR/ACR criteria, what total score is required to confirm definite Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: A score of ≥ 6 points is required for a definite diagnosis of RA.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1088 (Book Page): [Box 26.52] Patients with a score ≥ 6 are considered to have definite RA.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: How does the number of small joints involved affect the RA diagnostic score compared to large joints?
back:
Small joints are weighted higher:
- 1-3 small joints: 2 points.
- 4-10 small joints: 3 points.
- >10 joints (≥1 small): 5 points.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1088 (Book Page): [Box 26.52] 1–3 small joints (2); 4–10 small joints (3); > 10 joints (at least 1 small joint) (5).

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Which autoantibody has higher specificity for confirming Rheumatoid Arthritis than Rheumatoid Factor (RF)?
back: Anti-citrullinated peptide antibody (ACPA). It is highly specific and can appear before clinical symptom onset.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): Tests for ACPA are positive in about 70% of cases and are highly specific for RA, occurring in many patients before clinical onset of the disease.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: A patient has 5 small joints involved (3 points) and high-positive RF (3 points). Does this meet RA criteria?
back: Yes. The total score is 6, meeting the minimum threshold of ≥ 6 for definite RA.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1088 (Book Page): [Box 26.52] 4–10 small joints (3); High positive RF or ACPA (3). Patients with a score ≥ 6 are considered to have definite RA.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: What is the scoring contribution of abnormal ESR or CRP in the RA classification criteria?
back: Presence of either abnormal ESR or CRP contributes 1 point to the diagnostic total.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1088 (Book Page): [Box 26.52] Abnormal CRP or ESR (1).

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: What minimum duration of symptoms is required to score 1 point in the RA criteria?
back: Symptoms must persist for ≥ 6 weeks.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1088 (Book Page): [Box 26.52] Duration of symptoms... ≥ 6 weeks (1).

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Which imaging modalities are preferred for detecting synovitis in early RA when clinical examination is uncertain?
back: Ultrasound and MRI. They are more sensitive than plain X-rays for early inflammatory changes.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): Ultrasound examination and MRI... can be of value in patients with symptoms suggestive of RA where there is clinical uncertainty about the presence of synovitis.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Differentiate the hand joint distribution of RA from Nodal Osteoarthritis.
back: RA targets PIPs, MCPs, and wrists symmetrically. OA targets DIPs (Heberden's nodes) and PIPs (Bouchard's nodes).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): symmetrical fashion... small joints of the hands, feet and wrists. Page 1074 (Book Page): OA... targeting the hips, knees, PIP and DIP joints.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: What is the significance of the DAS28 score in RA management?
back: It assesses disease activity (Swollen/Tender counts, ESR/CRP, Patient assessment) to guide treatment and biologic eligibility.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): The Disease Activity Score in 28 joints (DAS28) is widely used to assess disease activity, response to treatment and need for biologic therapy.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: What are the characteristic X-ray findings in advanced Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back:
- Periarticular osteoporosis
- Marginal joint erosions
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): periarticular osteoporosis and marginal joint erosions may be observed with more advanced disease.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: What are the four core categories in the 2010 ACR/EULAR classification criteria for RA?
back:
• Joint involvement
• Serology (RF/ACPA)
• Acute-phase reactants (ESR/CRP)
• Duration of symptoms
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1028 (Book Page): [Table 26.52] Criteria for diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis: Joints affected, Serology, Duration of symptoms, Acute phase reactants.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Which specific genetic variant holds the strongest association with Rheumatoid Arthritis susceptibility?
back:
• HLA-DRβ1 molecule
• Specifically variations at positions 11, 71, and 74
• Also involves HLA-B (pos 9) and HLA-DPβ1 (pos 9)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1027 (Book Page): The strongest association is with variants in the HLA region and is determined by variations in three amino acids in the HLA-DRβ1 molecule (positions 11, 71 and 74).

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Contrast the diagnostic utility of ACPA versus Rheumatoid Factor (RF) in RA.
back:
• ACPA: Highly specific (>95%), appears before clinical onset
• RF: Less specific, found in other diseases (e.g., Sjögrēn’s)
• Both are ~70% sensitive
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1030 (Book Page): Tests for ACPA... are highly specific for RA... RF is less specific than ACPA, however, and positive tests can occur in other diseases.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: A patient has 4 small joints involved, high-positive ACPA, and 8-week symptom duration. Confirm RA?
back:
• Yes, definite RA (Score: 7)
• Small joints (4-10) = 3 pts
• High ACPA = 3 pts
• Duration (>6wks) = 1 pt
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1028 (Book Page): Patients with a score ≥ 6 are considered to have definite RA.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Which cytokine triggers the positive feedback loop between synovial macrophages and fibroblasts in RA?
back:
• TNF-α (primary activator)
• IL-1 and IL-6 (pro-inflammatory output)
• Leads to matrix metalloproteinase release and cartilage degradation
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1027 (Book Page): Macrophages produce several pro-inflammatory cytokines, including TNF-α, IL-1 and IL-6, which act on synovial fibroblasts... setting up a positive feedback loop.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: What is the minimum score required on ACR/EULAR criteria to confirm definite Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: • A score of ≥ 6 out of 10
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1028 (Book Page): Patients with a score ≥ 6 are considered to have definite RA.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: How does RA-related bone erosion occur at the joint margin?
back:
• Synovial 'pannus' invades bone
• Osteoclast activation via RANKL (from T-cells)
• M-CSF stimulation by synovial cells
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1027 (Book Page): A key pathogenic factor in bone erosions and periarticular osteoporosis is osteoclast activation, stimulated by the production of M-CSF by synovial cells and RANKL by activated T cells.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Distinguish RA from Polymyalgia Rheumatica in an elderly patient presenting with morning stiffness.
back:
• RA: True synovitis (swelling), ACPA/RF positive, small joints
• PMR: Proximal muscle stiffness, no true joint swelling, seronegative
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1027 (Book Page): Another presentation [of RA] is with proximal muscle stiffness mimicking polymyalgia rheumatica.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: What is the defining systemic loop initiated by IL-6 release in Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back:
• IL-6 triggers the liver to produce acute-phase proteins
• Results in elevated CRP and ESR
• Correlates with systemic disease activity
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1027 (Book Page): Systemic release of IL-6 triggers production of acute phase proteins by the liver.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: What are the characteristic early radiographic features of Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back:
• Periarticular osteoporosis
• Soft tissue swelling
• Marginal joint erosions (later finding)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1030 (Book Page): Plain X-rays of the hands, wrist and feet are usually normal in early RA, but periarticular osteoporosis and marginal joint erosions may be observed.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: What four categories constitute the 2010 EULAR/ACR classification criteria for Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back:
- Joint involvement (number/size)
- Serology (RF/ACPA)
- Symptom duration (≥6 weeks)
- Acute phase reactants (CRP/ESR)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Box 26.52] Criteria for diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis... Joints affected, Serology, Duration of symptoms, Acute phase reactants.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: How does the citrullination process relate to the pathophysiology of diagnostic RA serology?
back: Environmental triggers (e.g., smoking) modify host proteins via citrullination. These modified proteins become immunogenic, triggering production of highly specific Anti-Citrullinated Peptide Antibodies (ACPA).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Pathophysiology] ...triggering autoimmunity... by modifying host proteins, through processes like citrullination, so that they become immunogenic.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Contrast Rheumatoid Factor (RF) and Anti-Citrullinated Peptide Antibody (ACPA) in diagnostic specificity.
back:
- Both: ~70% sensitivity.
- ACPA: Highly specific for RA; often appears before clinical onset.
- RF: Less specific; also occurs in other inflammatory diseases.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): [Investigations] Tests for ACPA are positive in about 70% of cases and are highly specific for RA... RF is less specific than ACPA.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: A patient has symmetrical wrist/MCP swelling for 8 weeks and ACPA positivity. Confirm the diagnosis.
back: Definite Rheumatoid Arthritis. The symmetrical small joint involvement, duration >6 weeks, and high-positive serology exceed the EULAR/ACR score threshold of ≥6/10.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Clinical features] typical presentation is with pain, joint swelling and stiffness affecting the small joints of the hands... in a symmetrical fashion... score ≥ 6 are considered to have definite RA.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: What is the diagnostic significance of the 'shared epitope' in the HLA-DRβ1 molecule?
back: It represents the strongest genetic association with RA, determined by variations at positions 11, 71, and 74, influencing disease susceptibility and antibody production.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Pathophysiology] The strongest association is with variants in the HLA region and is determined by variations in three amino acids in the HLA-DRβ1 molecule (positions 11, 71 and 74).

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: What is the minimum EULAR/ACR 2010 score required to confirm a diagnosis of definite RA?
back: A total score of 6 or more out of 10 points is required across the classification domains.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Box 26.52] Patients with a score ≥ 6 are considered to have definite RA.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: How is joint involvement scored if more than 10 joints (including one small joint) are affected?
back: This degree of involvement is assigned the maximum score of 5 points in the 2010 criteria.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Box 26.52] > 10 joints (at least 1 small joint) = 5 [points].

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Differentiate the characteristic hand joint involvement of RA from nodal Osteoarthritis.
back:
- RA: Symmetrical MCP, PIP, and wrist involvement; characteristically spares DIP joints.
- Nodal OA: Targets DIP (Heberden's) and PIP (Bouchard's) joints.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1088 (Book Page): [Clinical features] Characteristics... include ulnar deviation of the fingers, ‘swan neck’ deformity... Page 1074 (Book Page): [Nodal OA] pain, stiffness and swelling of one or more PIP and DIP joints.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Which specific cytokine drives the acute phase response and raised CRP in confirmed RA?
back: Systemic release of Interleukin-6 (IL-6) triggers the liver to produce acute-phase proteins like CRP.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Pathophysiology] Systemic release of IL-6 triggers production of acute phase proteins by the liver.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: What are the two hallmark early radiographic features of RA on plain X-ray?
back:
1. Periarticular osteoporosis
2. Marginal joint erosions
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): [Investigations] periarticular osteoporosis and marginal joint erosions may be observed with more advanced disease.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Which investigation confirms a diagnosis of Gout?
back: Identification of needle-shaped, negatively birefringent monosodium urate crystals in synovial fluid aspirated from a joint, bursa, or tophus.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1079 (Book Page): The diagnosis of gout can be conﬁrmed by the identiﬁcation of urate crystals in the aspirate fr om a joint, bursa or tophus.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Interpret a normal serum uric acid level during an acute gout flare.
back: Urate levels often fall during inflammation; a normal level does not exclude an acute attack. Serial levels or joint aspiration are preferred.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1079 (Book Page): Hyperuricaemia is usually pr esent in gout, but levels may be normal during an attack because serum urate falls during inﬂammation.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Contrast the microscopic appearance of CPPD crystals vs. Gout crystals.
back: CPPD: Rhomboid/brick-shaped, weakly positively birefringent. Gout: Needle-shaped, strongly negatively birefringent.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1081 (Book Page): ...demonstrate CPP crystals (see Fig. 26.6B). [Implicit comparison in diagnostic sections for Gout vs CPPD]

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Which imaging is most sensitive for early sacroiliitis in Axial Spondyloarthritis (axSpA)?
back: MRI of the sacroiliac joints (STIR sequence) to detect bone marrow oedema (osteitis) before X-ray changes occur.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1093 (Book Page): MRI is mor e sensitive for detection of early sacr oiliitis than X-rays (see Fig. 26.40) and can also detect inﬂammatory changes in the lumbar spine.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: List mandatory baseline investigations before initiating Methotrexate (MTX) in RA.
back:
• Full Blood Count (FBC)
• Liver Function Tests (LFTs)
• Renal Function Tests (Urea/Creatinine)
• Chest X-ray
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): To monitor drug safety: Urinalysis, Urea and creatinine, Full blood count, Liver function tests, Chest X-ray.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Compare the diagnostic significance of Anti-CCP (ACPA) vs. Rheumatoid Factor (RF) in RA.
back: Anti-CCP is highly specific for RA (approx. 70%) and often precedes symptoms. RF is sensitive but less specific (found in other diseases).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): Tests for ACPA ar e positive in about 70% of cases and ar e highly speciﬁc for RA, occur ring in many patients befor e clinical onset of the disease.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Interpret a 'halo' sign on temporal artery Doppler ultrasound.
back: Indicates a thickened, oedematous vessel wall; highly suggestive of Giant Cell Arteritis (GCA).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1046 (Book Page): The characteristic ﬁnding on Doppler ultrasound examination is the ‘halo’ sign, wher e the thickened vessel wall shows as a dark ar ea sur rounding a positive Doppler signal within the vessel.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Interpret significantly elevated CRP in a patient with SLE flare (normally normal).
back: Presence of high CRP in active SLE suggests either serositis (e.g., pleurisy/pericarditis) or a co-existing infection.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1099 (Book Page): CRP is often normal in active SLE and pr esence of an elevated CRP in SLE raises the possibility of either ser ositis, or co-existing infection.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: What mandatory screening is required in newly diagnosed adult-onset Dermatomyositis (DM)?
back: Screening for underlying malignancy (CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, mammography, PSA, pelvic exam).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1102 (Book Page): Scr eening for under lying malignancy should be under taken r outinely (full examination, chest X-ray, serum urine and pr otein electr ophoresis, CT of chest/abdomen/pelvis).

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Identify the characteristic biochemical finding in Adult-onset Still’s Disease.
back: Markedly elevated serum ferritin levels alongside a raised ESR and CRP.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1103 (Book Page): Investigations typically pr ovide evidence of an acute phase r esponse with raised ESR and CRP and a markedly elevated serum ferritin.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
coreConcept: Synovial Fluid Analysis in Crystal Arthropathies
front: Q: What is the definitive investigation to confirm a diagnosis of Gout?
back: Identification of monosodium urate crystals in synovial fluid, which are needle-shaped and negatively birefringent under polarized microscopy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1079 (Book Page): The diagnosis of gout can be confirmed by the identification of urate crystals in the aspirate from a joint, bursa or tophus.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Contrast the polarized microscopy findings of Monosodium Urate vs. Calcium Pyrophosphate crystals.
back:
Urate (Gout): Needle-shaped, negatively birefringent.
CPP (Pseudogout): Rhomboid-shaped, positively birefringent.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1081 (Book Page): demonstrate CPP crystals (see Fig. 26.6B) ... compensated polarised microscopy.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Which investigation is most sensitive for detecting early sacroiliitis in Axial Spondyloarthritis?
back: MRI of the sacroiliac joints, specifically looking for bone marrow oedema (osteitis) on STIR sequences.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1093 (Book Page): Inflammatory changes in the axial skeleton (such as sacroiliitis... ) are characteristic of axSpA and are visualised by MRI.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Interpret the clinical significance of anti-dsDNA and C3/C4 levels in SLE management.
back: Anti-dsDNA is highly specific for SLE diagnosis; low C3/C4 levels indicate complement consumption during active disease flares.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1100 (Book Page): Anti-dsDNA antibodies are positive in most patients and are quite specific for SLE. Serum levels of C3 may be low in active SLE due to complement consumption.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What are the four hallmark radiological features of Osteoarthritis on a plain X-ray?
back:
1. Joint space narrowing
2. Subchondral sclerosis
3. Osteophyte formation
4. Subchondral cysts
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1073 (Book Page): Characterised by focal loss of articular cartilage, subchondral osteosclerosis, osteophyte formation at the joint margin and remodelling.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Which autoantibodies are most specific for diagnosing Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: Anti-citrullinated peptide antibodies (ACPA/Anti-CCP), which are more specific than Rheumatoid Factor and can precede clinical onset.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): Tests for ACPA are positive in about 70% of cases and are highly specific for RA, occurring in many patients before clinical onset.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: In Systemic Sclerosis, which antibody is specifically associated with the Limited (CREST) subtype?
back: Anticentromere antibodies (found in approximately 60% of limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis cases).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1101 (Book Page): About 60% of patients have anticentromere antibodies and this is a biomarker for lcSScl and CREST syndrome.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Define the 'halo sign' seen on Doppler ultrasound in a suspected Giant Cell Arteritis patient.
back: Dark area of vessel wall thickening (oedema) surrounding a positive Doppler signal, indicating active arterial inflammation.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1106 (Book Page): Characteristic finding on Doppler ultrasound examination is the ‘halo’ sign, where the thickened vessel wall shows as a dark area surrounding a positive Doppler signal.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What parameters are measured to calculate the DAS28 score for monitoring Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: Number of swollen joints, number of tender joints, ESR or CRP, and patient global health visual analogue score.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): It involves counting the number of swollen and tender joints in the upper limbs and knees, and combining this with the ESR and the patient’s assessment.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What is the pivotal investigation for suspected Polymyositis or Dermatomyositis?
back: Muscle biopsy, showing fiber necrosis, regeneration, and inflammatory cell infiltrate, often guided by prior MRI (STIR).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1103 (Book Page): Muscle biopsy is the pivotal investigation and shows the typical features of fibre necrosis, regeneration and inflammatory cell infiltrate.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: List the four hallmark radiological features of Osteoarthritis seen on a plain X-ray.
back: 1. Focal joint space narrowing; 2. Subchondral osteosclerosis; 3. Osteophyte formation; 4. Subchondral cysts.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1073 (Book Page): Osteoarthritis (OA) ... is characterised by focal loss of articular cartilage, subchondral osteosclerosis, osteophyte formation at the joint margin and remodelling of joint contour.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Why might serum uric acid levels appear normal during an acute flare of Gout?
back: Serum urate levels frequently fall during acute inflammation because uric acid is deposited into joints or rapidly excreted.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1079 (Book Page): Hyperuricaemia is usually present in gout, but levels may be normal during an attack because serum urate falls during inflammation.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Contrast the microscopic appearance of Monosodium Urate (MSU) vs Calcium Pyrophosphate (CPP) crystals.
back: 1. MSU (Gout): Needle-shaped, strong negative birefringence; 2. CPP (Pseudogout): Rhomboid/brick-shaped, weak positive birefringence.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1081 (Book Page): demonstrate CPP crystals (see Fig. 26.6B) ... identification of urate crystals (see Fig. 26.6A).

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: An RA patient presents with occipital headache and arm paresthesia. What is the most urgent investigation?
back: Lateral cervical spine X-rays in flexion/extension and an MRI to diagnose atlanto-axial subluxation and potential cord compression.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): It should be suspected in any RA patient who describes new onset of occipital headache ... patients who are suspected of having atlanto-axial disease should have lateral X-rays taken in flexion and extension, and an MRI.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What laboratory tests are mandatory for safety monitoring in a patient taking Methotrexate?
back: 1. Full Blood Count (FBC); 2. Liver Function Tests (LFTs); 3. Urea and Creatinine (Renal function).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): To monitor drug safety: Urinalysis, Urea and creatinine, Full blood count, Liver function tests.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: According to the CASPAR criteria, what is the score required to diagnose Psoriatic Arthritis?
back: A score of 3 points or more from categories like current psoriasis, nail dystrophy, negative RF, and current/history of dactylitis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1096 (Book Page): The CASPAR criteria for psoriatic arthritis ... with ≥ 3 points from the following...

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What is the pivotal investigation for suspected Septic Arthritis?
back: Urgent joint aspiration for synovial fluid Gram stain and culture (90% sensitivity).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1084 (Book Page): The pivotal investigation is joint aspiration ... Synovial fluid should be sent for Gram stain and culture; cultures are positive in around 90% of cases.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: A patient with sinusitis and hemoptysis has a positive c-ANCA (PR3). What is the diagnosis?
back: Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (GPA), formerly Wegener's granulomatosis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1104 (Book Page): Patients with GPA are usually proteinase-3 (PR3) antibody-positive ... most common presentation ... is with epistaxis, nasal crusting and sinusitis, but haemoptysis ... may also occur.

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: What does a low C3/C4 complement level signify in a patient with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)?
back: Indicates disease activity or flares, reflecting complement consumption by circulating immune complexes.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1100 (Book Page): Serum levels of C3 may be low in active SLE due to complement consumption...

category: Interpret relevant investigations
front: Q: Which specific autoantibody is the best diagnostic marker for Rheumatoid Arthritis due to its high specificity?
back: Anti-citrullinated peptide antibody (ACPA or Anti-CCP).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): Tests for ACPA are positive in about 70% of cases and are highly specific for RA.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Which specific classification system is used as the current international standard for diagnosing Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: The EULAR/ACR 2010 criteria (European League Against Rheumatism/American College of Rheumatology).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1088 (Book Page): [European League Against Rheumatism/American College of Rheumatology 2010 criteria.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: How does the process of citrullination facilitate the diagnostic serology found in Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: Environmental triggers modify host proteins (citrullination), making them immunogenic. This stimulates production of highly specific Anti-Citrullinated Peptide Antibodies (ACPA).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [triggering autoimmunity... by modifying host proteins, through processes like citrullination, so that they become immunogenic.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: What distinguishes the joint distribution of RA from OA regarding small joints of the hand?
back: RA typically affects MCP and PIP joints symmetrically, sparing the DIPs, while OA characteristically targets DIPs and PIPs.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1088 (Book Page): [symmetrical fashion... metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: A patient has 3 small joint swellings, high-positive RF, and symptoms for 4 weeks. Calculate the ACR/EULAR score.
back: Score: 5. (Small joints = 2; High positive RF = 3; <6 weeks duration = 0). Definite RA requires ≥ 6.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1088 (Book Page): [1–3 small joints 2... High positive RF or ACPA 3... < 6 weeks 0... Patients with a score ≥ 6 are considered to have definite RA.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Why is IL-6 a critical cytokine in the diagnostic laboratory workup for suspected Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: Systemic IL-6 release triggers the liver to produce acute-phase proteins, manifesting as elevated ESR and CRP levels in labs.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Systemic release of IL-6 triggers production of acute phase proteins by the liver.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: What is the minimum threshold score on the 2010 ACR/EULAR criteria to confirm definite RA?
back: A total score of 6 or higher out of 10.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1088 (Book Page): [Patients with a score ≥ 6 are considered to have definite RA.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Which four assessment categories comprise the 2010 EULAR/ACR classification criteria for Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: 1. Joint involvement. 2. Serology (RF/ACPA). 3. Acute phase reactants (ESR/CRP). 4. Duration of symptoms.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1088 (Book Page): [Joints affected... Serology... Duration of symptoms... Acute phase reactants.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: How is the 'High Positive' serology score (3 points) defined in RA diagnostic criteria?
back: Autoantibody levels (RF or ACPA) that are more than three times the upper limit of normal.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1088 (Book Page): [Criteria for diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis... High positive RF or ACPA 3]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: What role does symptom duration of ≥ 6 weeks play in the EULAR/ACR diagnostic score?
back: It adds 1 point to the score, helping differentiate chronic RA from transient viral polyarthritis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1088 (Book Page): [Duration of symptoms... > 6 weeks 1]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Which serum autoantibody is considered more specific for a diagnosis of Rheumatoid Arthritis than Rheumatoid Factor?
back: Anti-Citrullinated Peptide Antibody (ACPA).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): [Tests for ACPA are positive in about 70% of cases and are highly specific for RA.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: What is the minimum score required to confirm a diagnosis of Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA)?
back: A score of 6 or higher (out of a possible 10).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Criteria for diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis] Patients with a score ≥ 6 are considered to have definite RA.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: How does protein citrullination trigger the autoimmune response in Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: Environmental triggers (e.g., smoking) modify host proteins via citrullination, making them immunogenic to the immune system in genetically susceptible individuals.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [RA occurs when an environmental stimulus] triggers autoimmunity in a genetically susceptible host by modifying host proteins, through processes like citrullination, so that they become immunogenic.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Contrast the diagnostic utility of Rheumatoid Factor (RF) versus Anti-ACPA in RA diagnosis.
back: Anti-ACPA is highly specific for RA and often present before clinical onset; RF is less specific and occurs in other diseases.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): Tests for ACPA are positive in about 70% of cases and are highly specific for RA... RF is less specific than ACPA, however, and positive tests can occur in other diseases.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Clinical Scenario: Patient has 5 small joints involved (3wks), high-positive ACPA, and normal ESR. Confirm diagnosis?
back: Confirmed. Score = 3 (4–10 small joints) + 3 (High ACPA) + 0 (Duration <6wks) + 0 (Normal ESR) = 6/10.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Box 26.52] 4–10 small joints (3) ... High positive RF or ACPA (3) ... Patients with a score ≥ 6 are considered to have definite RA.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: What is the initial standard DMARD drug of choice and starting dose for newly diagnosed RA?
back: Methotrexate (MTX) starting at 15mg weekly, escalated to a maximum of 25mg weekly.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1091 (Book Page): methotrexate (MTX) should be started in an initial dose of 15 mg weekly... and escalated up to a maximum of 25 mg weekly.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: List the four domains evaluated in the ACR/EULAR classification criteria for RA.
back: 1. Joint involvement; 2. Serology (RF/ACPA); 3. Duration of symptoms; 4. Acute phase reactants (CRP/ESR).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Box 26.52 Criteria for diagnosis] Joints affected, Serology, Duration of symptoms, Acute phase reactants.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: What duration of joint symptoms is required to score 1 point in RA diagnostic criteria?
back: Symptoms persisting for 6 weeks or longer.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Duration of symptoms] < 6 weeks (0), ≥ 6 weeks (1).

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
coreConcept: Differential Diagnosis of Soft Tissue Lumps
front: Q: How do you clinically differentiate Rheumatoid nodules from Gouty tophi?
back: Tophi are characterized by a white color and may discharge gritty material; Rheumatoid nodules are typically flesh-colored on extensor surfaces.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1079 (Book Page): Tophi have a white colour (Fig. 26.26), differentiating them from rheumatoid nodules.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Which specific cytokines set up the positive feedback loop between macrophages and fibroblasts in RA?
back: TNF-α, IL-1, and IL-6 produced by macrophages act on synovial fibroblasts.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): macrophages produce... TNF-α, IL-1 and IL-6, which act on synovial fibroblasts to produce further cytokines, setting up a positive feedback loop.

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Which specific amino acid positions on the HLA-DRβ1 molecule determine the strongest genetic risk for RA?
back: Positions 11, 71, and 74.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): variations in three amino acids in the HLA-DRβ1 molecule (positions 11, 71 and 74).

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Which specific joint groups are primarily targeted in the typical symmetrical presentation of Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: The small joints of the hands, feet, and wrists are primarily involved in a symmetrical distribution.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [The typical presentation is with pain, joint swelling and stiffness affecting the small joints of the hands, feet and wrists in a symmetrical fashion.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: How do synovial macrophages contribute to the inflammatory feedback loop in Rheumatoid Arthritis pathophysiology?
back: Macrophages produce cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1, IL-6) that activate synovial fibroblasts to produce further cytokines and matrix metalloproteinases.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [The macrophages produce several pro-inflammatory cytokines, including TNF-α, IL-1 and IL-6, which act on synovial fibroblasts to produce further cytokines, setting up a positive feedback loop.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Contrast the diagnostic specificity of Rheumatoid Factor (RF) versus Anti-Citrullinated Peptide Antibodies (ACPA) in RA.
back: ACPA is highly specific for RA and often appears before clinical onset, whereas RF is less specific and occurs in other diseases.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): [Tests for ACPA are positive in about 70% of cases and are highly specific for RA... RF is less specific than ACPA, however, and positive tests can occur in other diseases.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: A patient with long-standing RA presents with new occipital headache and arm paraesthesia. What must be excluded?
back: Atlanto-axial subluxation causing spinal cord compression due to erosion of the transverse ligament behind the odontoid peg.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): [It should be suspected in any RA patient who describes new onset of occipital headache, particularly if symptoms of paraesthesia or electric shock are present in the arms.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: What is the pharmacological rationale for co-prescribing Folic Acid with Methotrexate in RA treatment?
back: Folic acid is administered (typically 5mg weekly) to reduce methotrexate-associated side effects and systemic toxicity.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1090 (Book Page): [methotrexate (MTX) should be started in an initial dose of 15 mg weekly, along with folic acid 5 mg weekly.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: According to the 2010 ACR/EULAR criteria, what total score confirms a diagnosis of definite Rheumatoid Arthritis?
back: A total score of 6 or greater (≥ 6) is required for definitive diagnosis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1087 (Book Page): [Patients with a score ≥ 6 are considered to have definite RA.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
front: Q: Which parameters are combined to calculate the Disease Activity Score 28 (DAS28) in RA monitoring?
back: It combines swollen/tender joint counts (upper limbs/knees), ESR or CRP levels, and the patient's global health visual analogue score.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 1089 (Book Page): [It involves counting the number of swollen and tender joints... combining this with the ESR and the patient’s assessment of the activity of their arthritis.]

category: Discuss the diagnostic criteria for confirming RA
